In 2018, Omar ran for the U.S. House of Representatives and won, becoming the first Somali American elected to Congress. She has been a vocal advocate for progressive policies, including a $15 minimum wage, universal healthcare, and student loan debt forgiveness. Omar has also been a critic of Israel, supporting the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) movement and denouncing Israel's settlement policies.

As a member of Congress, Omar has introduced several bills, including a resolution supporting the right to boycotts and a bill to designate a post office in Minneapolis after Martin Olav Sabo. She has also been a vocal critic of former President Donald Trump, leading a group of lawmakers in introducing articles of impeachment against him in 2021.

Omar's committee assignments include the Committee on Education and the Workforce and the Committee on the Budget. She is also a member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and the Congressional Black Caucus. Omar has been a vocal advocate for social justice and has spoken out on issues such as racial equality, immigration reform, and women's rights.

Throughout her career, Omar has received numerous awards and recognition for her advocacy and public service. She has been named one of Time Magazine's 100 Most Influential People in the World and has received the American Civil Liberties Union's (ACLU) Champion of Civil Liberties Award.

Despite facing controversy and criticism, Omar has remained a committed advocate for progressive policies and social justice. Her experiences as a refugee and a woman of color have informed her approach to politics and have driven her to push for change in her community and in Congress.

title: Nelson Mandela
text:
Nelson Mandela was a South African anti-apartheid activist and politician who served as the country's first black president from 1994 to 1999. Born on July 18, 1918, in the village of Mvezo, South Africa, Mandela was given the forename Rolihlahla, which means "troublemaker" in Xhosa. His patrilineal great-grandfather, Ngubengcuka, was the ruler of the Thembu Kingdom in the Transkeian Territories of South Africa's modern Eastern Cape province.

Mandela's early life was dominated by traditional Xhosa custom and taboo. He grew up in a polygamous family and was sent to a local Methodist school at the age of seven, where he was baptized a Methodist and given the English forename of "Nelson." After his father's death, Mandela was entrusted to the guardianship of the Thembu regent, Chief Jongintaba Dalindyebo, who raised him alongside his own children.

Mandela attended several schools, including Clarkebury Methodist High School and Healdtown, a Methodist college in Fort Beaufort. He later attended the University of Fort Hare, where he studied English, anthropology, politics, and Roman Dutch law. However, he was suspended from the university for participating in a students' representative council boycott, and he never returned to complete his degree.

In 1941, Mandela moved to Johannesburg, where he found work as a night watchman and later as an articled clerk at a law firm. He became involved in the African National Congress (ANC) and joined the ANC Youth League, which he co-founded in 1944. Mandela's involvement in the ANC led to his appointment as a president of the ANC's Transvaal branch, and he played a key role in the 1952 Defiance Campaign and the 1955 Congress of the People.

Mandela's activism led to his arrest and imprisonment several times. In 1962, he was arrested and sentenced to life imprisonment for conspiring to overthrow the state. He spent 27 years in prison, including 18 years on Robben Island, where he was subjected to hard labor and mistreatment. Despite his imprisonment, Mandela continued to advocate for an end to apartheid and was released from prison in 1990 after international pressure.

After his release, Mandela played a key role in negotiating an end to apartheid, and in 1994, he became the first black president of South Africa, leading the ANC to victory in the country's first multiracial democratic election. As president, Mandela focused on dismantling the legacy of apartheid and fostering racial reconciliation. He established the Truth and Reconciliation Commission to investigate past human rights abuses and introduced measures to promote economic development and social justice.

Mandela's presidency was marked by his efforts to promote national unity and reconciliation. He worked with his predecessor, F.W. de Klerk, and other leaders to establish a new constitution and promote economic development. He also played a key role in international diplomacy, acting as a mediator in the Pan Am Flight 103 bombing trial and serving as secretary-general of the Non-Aligned Movement.

After leaving office in 1999, Mandela continued to work on various humanitarian projects, including combating poverty and HIV/AIDS. He received over 250 honors, including the Nobel Peace Prize, and was widely regarded as an icon of democracy and social justice. Mandela passed away on December 5, 2013, at the age of 95, leaving behind a legacy as a champion of human rights and social justice.

title: Joey Jordison
text:
Nathan Jonas "Joey" Jordison was a renowned American musician, best known as the original drummer of the heavy metal band Slipknot, where he was designated #1. He was also the guitarist for the horror punk supergroup Murderdolls. Jordison grew up in Des Moines, Iowa, with his parents and two sisters, and developed a passion for music from an early age. His parents encouraged his interest in music, often playing the radio instead of TV, which exposed him to various artists and bands.

Jordison's introduction to drumming came when he received his first drum kit at the age of eight. He quickly became fascinated with music and formed his first band, Modifidious, while in elementary school. As he grew older, Jordison played with several bands before joining the Pale Ones in 1995, which later became Slipknot. He was the third member to join the band, and his unique drumming style, which incorporated custom percussionists, helped shape Slipknot's sound.

With Slipknot, Jordison performed on the band's first five studio albums, including "Slipknot", "Iowa", "Vol. 3: (The Subliminal Verses)", "All Hope Is Gone", and "5". He also produced the live album "9.0: Live" in 2005. Jordison's work with Slipknot was marked by his energetic stage presence and his ability to play complex drum patterns.

In addition to his work with Slipknot, Jordison was involved in several side projects. He formed the Murderdolls in 2002, with Tripp Eisen and Wednesday 13, and released two studio albums, "Beyond the Valley of the Murderdolls" and "Women and Children Last". Jordison also collaborated with other artists, such as Rob Zombie, Metallica, Korn, Ministry, and Otep, and performed with various bands as a touring member.

Jordison's career was marked by his versatility and his ability to adapt to different musical styles. He was known for his session work, and his credits include performances on recordings for many artists. Jordison was also a producer, and he worked on several albums, including 3 Inches of Blood's "Fire Up the Blades".

In 2010, Jordison was voted the best drummer of the previous 25 years by readers of Rhythm magazine, and he won the Drummies Award for Best Metal drummer. He was also named the world's greatest metal drummer by readers of Loudwire in 2013.

Despite his success, Jordison faced health challenges, including transverse myelitis, a neurological disease that affected his ability to play the drums. He underwent rehabilitation and recovered, but the experience had a lasting impact on his life. Jordison passed away on July 26, 2021, at the age of 46, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most influential drummers in heavy metal music.

Throughout his career, Jordison was known for his technical skill, energetic stage presence, and versatility. He was a respected figure in the music industry, and his contributions to Slipknot, Murderdolls, and other projects continue to inspire and influence musicians to this day. Jordison's legacy extends beyond his music, as he helped to shape the sound of heavy metal in the 1990s and 2000s. His impact on the music industry will be remembered for years to come.

title: Muhammad Qutb
text:
Muhammad Qutb was a renowned Islamic scholar born on April 26, 1919, in the Upper Egyptian village of Musha near Asyut. He was the younger brother of Sayyid Qutb, a prominent Egyptian revolutionary. Muhammad was the second oldest of five children, and his family moved to Helwan near Cairo after their father's death in 1933. He studied English literature at Cairo University, graduating in 1940, and later obtained diplomas in psychology and education.

In 1965, Muhammad was arrested along with his brother on charges of co-leading a plot to kill leading political and cultural figures in Egypt and overthrow the government. While his brother was hanged in 1966, Muhammad's life was spared, and he took refuge in Saudi Arabia. There, he edited and published his brother's books, including the influential work "Milestones." Muhammad also taught as a professor of Islamic Studies at Umm al-Qura University and King Abdulaziz University, where notable students included Osama bin Laden and Ayman al-Zawahiri.

Muhammad worked to advance his brother's ideas while "smoothing away" differences between his brother's radical supporters and more conservative Muslims. He took a less-literal interpretation of his brother's statement that the Muslim world and Muslim governments were jahiliyya, or returned to pagan ignorance. In 1975, Muhammad publicly opposed takfir, or judging Muslims as unbelievers. He also sought to reconcile the doctrine of the Muslim Brotherhood with the salafism prevalent in Saudi Arabia.

Muhammad was a prolific author, writing 36 books, including "Islam: The Misunderstood Religion" and "Jahiliyat al-qarn al-ishrin" (Jahiliyya of the Twentieth Century). His views on various topics, including anti-Semitism, slavery, and feminism, have been influential in shaping 20th-century Muslim thought. He criticized Western cultural imperialism and portrayed it as a threat to Muslim society, often using anti-Semitic conspiracy theories. Muhammad defended Islamic slavery, comparing it favorably to slavery in the West.

Muhammad's influence extended beyond his academic position, as he held private teaching circles and disseminated his lectures through cassettes, pamphlets, and the internet. One of his most famous students was Safar al-Hawali, a key figure in the Sahwa movement. Muhammad played a significant role in promoting his brother's work and ideas, and his own writings continue to be widely read in the Arab world.

Muhammad Qutb passed away on April 4, 2014, at the age of 94, in a hospital in Mecca. His legacy as a prominent Islamic scholar and advocate for Muslim Brotherhood ideology continues to be felt, with his ideas influencing a new generation of Muslim thinkers and activists.

title: Ayman al-Zawahiri
text:
Ayman Mohammed Rabie al-Zawahiri was an Egyptian-born pan-Islamist militant and physician who played a significant role in the global terrorist network. Born on June 19, 1951, in Giza, Egypt, al-Zawahiri came from a prestigious family with a strong background in medicine and politics. His father, Mohammed Rabie al-Zawahiri, was a surgeon and professor of pharmacy at Cairo University, and his mother, Umayma Azzam, came from a wealthy and influential family.

Al-Zawahiri's early life was marked by his studious nature and his interest in Islamist ideology. He studied medicine at Cairo University, graduating in 1974, and later earned a master's degree in surgery in 1978. During his time at university, he became involved in Islamist activism and formed an underground cell with the goal of overthrowing the government and establishing an Islamist state.

In 1981, al-Zawahiri was arrested and imprisoned for his role in the assassination of Egyptian President Anwar Sadat. He was tortured in prison, but was released in 1984. After his release, he traveled to Peshawar, Pakistan, where he worked in a Red Crescent hospital treating wounded refugees and became friends with Ahmed Khadr.

Al-Zawahiri's militant activities continued, and he became a key figure in the Egyptian Islamic Jihad (EIJ). He was involved in several plots, including the 1995 attack on the Egyptian Embassy in Islamabad, Pakistan, and the 1998 U.S. embassy bombings in Kenya and Tanzania. He also became a close associate of Osama bin Laden and played a significant role in the merger of the EIJ with al-Qaeda in 2001.

In 2001, al-Zawahiri became the deputy leader of al-Qaeda, and after bin Laden's death in 2011, he succeeded him as the leader of the organization. As leader, al-Zawahiri continued to plan and inspire terrorist attacks, including the 2012 Benghazi attack.

Al-Zawahiri was married at least four times and had several children. His first wife, Azza Ahmed Nowari, and their children were killed in a U.S. airstrike in Afghanistan in 2001. He was also known to have written several books and articles on Islamist ideology and to have given numerous interviews to Arabic-language media outlets.

On July 31, 2022, al-Zawahiri was killed in a CIA drone strike in Afghanistan. The strike was a significant blow to al-Qaeda and marked a major achievement for the U.S. counterterrorism efforts. Al-Zawahiri's legacy as a militant and ideologue continues to be felt, and his actions and writings remain a subject of study and concern for scholars, policymakers, and law enforcement agencies around the world.

Throughout his life, al-Zawahiri was known for his charisma and his ability to inspire loyalty among his followers. He was also known for his strategic thinking and his ability to adapt to changing circumstances. Despite his death, al-Zawahiri's impact on the global terrorist landscape is likely to be felt for years to come.

Al-Zawahiri's story is a complex and multifaceted one, reflecting the nuances and contradictions of his life and legacy. He was a physician who became a militant, a ideologue who became a leader, and a man who was driven by a desire to change the world. His life and actions serve as a reminder of the ongoing threat posed by terrorist organizations and the need for continued vigilance and cooperation in the face of this threat.

title: Diego Suarez (garden designer)
text:
Diego Suarez was a Colombian garden designer, diplomat, and architect who is best known for his work on Villa Vizcaya in Miami, Florida. Born in Bogotá, Colombia in 1888, Suarez was the son of a Colombian diplomat and historian, Roberto Suarez, and his Italian wife, Maria Costa. After his father's death, Suarez and his siblings spent their childhood in Italy, where Suarez studied architectural design at the Accademia delle Belle Arti in Florence.

During his time in Florence, Suarez was taken under the wing of Arthur Acton, a member of the English expatriate community, who was restoring the gardens of Villa La Pietra. Acton introduced Suarez to the Anglo-American community in Florence, where Suarez began to lay out gardens for various clients, including Lewis Einstein and Charles Loeser. In 1914, Suarez met James Deering, the heir to the International Harvester fortune, and his artistic advisor, Paul Chalfin, while they were on a tour of villas in Italy.

When Deering decided to create a garden at his new estate, Villa Vizcaya, in Miami, Florida, he hired Suarez to design the gardens. Suarez's design for Villa Vizcaya centered on two façades of the house, one facing Biscayne Bay and the other facing south. The gardens feature a boat basin, a central island, and a fountain that Suarez had purchased with Deering and Chalfin. The fountain, which was originally from Bassano di Sutri, near Viterbo, was a key element in the design and was sited at the end of a cross-axis, rather than in the central axis, to create a sense of discovery.

Suarez's design for Villa Vizcaya was influenced by the French baroque style, with parterres en broderie, contrasts of sun and shade, and many slight changes of level to enliven the flat site. The gardens were designed to be viewed from the house, with radiating side axes that offer glimpses of the lake beyond their ends.

In addition to his work as a garden designer, Suarez also had a career in diplomacy. From 1948 to 1952, he served as press attaché and minister-counselor for Chile in Washington, D.C. He also worked as counselor to the Colombian delegation to the United Nations.

In his personal life, Suarez married Evelyn Marshall Field in 1937, and they had three stepchildren together. Suarez died on September 14, 1974, in New York City, and is interred at Woodlawn Cemetery in The Bronx. In 1952, Suarez collaborated with architect Frederic Rhinelander King to complete a neoclassical house with extensive gardens at Brookville, New York. Throughout his life, Suarez was known for his skill as a garden designer and his ability to create beautiful and unique spaces that reflected his clients' personalities and styles.

title: Daniel Alexander Cameron
text:
Daniel Alexander Cameron was a Canadian politician from Nova Scotia who served in various capacities during the early 20th century. Born on December 10, 1870, in Sydney River, Nova Scotia, he was the son of John and Isabella Cameron. Cameron received his education at Sydney Academy and later at Dalhousie University, where he earned a Bachelor of Laws degree. He was admitted to the bar in 1893 and began practicing law in Sydney in 1894.

Cameron's entry into politics began with his appointment to the County Council, where he served from 1900 to 1911. During this time, he also held the position of stipendiary magistrate for Sydney from 1905 to 1911. In 1911, he was appointed as treasurer and solicitor for the Municipality of Cape Breton. His experience in local politics and law prepared him for his future roles in the provincial government.

In 1916, Cameron was elected to the Nova Scotia House of Assembly, representing the electoral district of Cape Breton. As a member of the Nova Scotia Liberal Party, he served in the assembly until his defeat in 1920. However, his time out of office was short-lived, as he was appointed to the Legislative Council of Nova Scotia in 1921. During this period, he also served as Minister Without Portfolio in the cabinet of George Henry Murray.

Cameron's tenure in the Legislative Council was brief, as he resigned in 1923 and was elected to the House of Assembly for Victoria County. He then served as Provincial Secretary in the cabinet of Ernest Howard Armstrong from 1923 to 1925. After a brief stint out of politics, Cameron ran as the Liberal candidate for the electoral district of Cape Breton South in the 1930 federal election but was defeated.

Cameron's final foray into politics came in 1935, when he was elected to the House of Assembly for the electoral district of Cape Breton North and Victoria. He served in this role for nearly two years before his death on September 4, 1937, making him one of the first Nova Scotian legislators of the 20th century to die while in office. Throughout his career, Cameron demonstrated his commitment to public service, holding various positions in local and provincial government.

title: Shin Jea-hwan
text:
Shin Jea-hwan is a South Korean artistic gymnast born on March 3, 1998, in Seoul. He attended the Korea National Sport University and graduated in 2020, after which he relocated to Jecheon in 2021. Shin's gymnastics career is on the rise, and his idol is teammate Yang Hak-seon.

Shin made his senior international debut at the 2019 Zhaoqing World Cup, where he won a silver medal on vault and finished fourth on floor exercise. He continued to compete on vault and floor at several events on the 2020 World Cup circuit, winning two gold medals on vault at the 2020 Melbourne and 2020 Baku World Cups. His strong performances on vault earned him a spot as the leader in the series to qualify for the 2020 Summer Olympics when the COVID-19 pandemic curtailed the 2020 series.

In 2021, Shin attended the 2021 Doha World Cup, a final event in the qualification process, to preserve his series lead over Japanese gymnast Hidenobu Yonekura. Despite placing fifth in the competition, Shin won the overall series on a tiebreaker and qualified as an individual for the Olympic Games in Tokyo.

At the 2020 Summer Olympics, Shin qualified for the vault final in first place, beating Armenia's Artur Davtyan in a tiebreak with both men scoring 14.866. In the vault final, he faced another tough competition from Denis Ablyazin of ROC, but won the gold medal after ranking ahead in the tiebreak once more. Both men scored 14.783, but Shin's higher individual vault score (14.833 vs 14.800) secured his victory. This gold medal is South Korea's second on the vault apparatus, after Yang Hak-seon won it at the 2012 Summer Olympics in London.

Throughout his career, Shin has demonstrated his skill and determination, and his Olympic gold medal is a testament to his hard work and dedication to the sport. With his achievements, Shin has made a name for himself in the gymnastics world and is considered one of the top gymnasts in South Korea.

title: Ivan Perišić
text:
Ivan Perišić is a Croatian professional footballer who plays as a winger for PSV. Born on February 2, 1989, he is considered one of the greatest Croatian players of all time. Perišić is known for his ambidexterity and versatility, having played in various positions including left winger, left wing-back, right winger, attacking midfielder, and second striker.

Perišić began his youth career at Hajduk Split, but moved to Sochaux in 2006. He failed to make a first-team appearance for Sochaux, but played for the B team. In 2009, he was loaned to Roeselare and later signed with Club Brugge. At Brugge, Perišić made a name for himself, scoring 22 goals in the 2010-2011 season and winning the Belgian Pro League top scorer award. He was also named Belgian Footballer of the Year for 2011.

Perišić's impressive performance at Brugge earned him a transfer to Borussia Dortmund, where he won the 2011-2012 Bundesliga title. He then moved to VfL Wolfsburg for €8 million in 2013, where he spent two and a half seasons and won the 2015 DFB-Pokal final.

In 2015, Perišić signed with Inter Milan for €16 million. During his time at Inter, he made 171 appearances, scoring 43 goals and providing 39 assists. Perišić helped Inter win the 2020-2021 Serie A title, the 2021 Supercoppa Italiana, and the 2021-2022 Coppa Italia.

In 2019, Perišić joined Bayern Munich on loan, where he won the treble, including the Champions League. After returning to Inter Milan, he continued to play an important role for the team.

Perišić has also been an important player for the Croatia national team, making his debut in 2011. He has represented Croatia in several major tournaments, including the UEFA European Championship and the FIFA World Cup. In the 2018 World Cup, Perišić scored an equalizing goal in the final against France.

Throughout his career, Perišić has been praised for his skills, work rate, and versatility. He has won numerous titles and individual awards, and has established himself as one of the top Croatian players of his generation.

Perišić has made 113 appearances for the Croatia national team, scoring 33 goals and providing 18 assists. He has been instrumental in Croatia's success in recent years, including their second-place finish in the 2018 World Cup.

In 2022, Perišić helped Croatia win a bronze medal at the World Cup. With his experience and skills, Perišić continues to be an important player for both club and country.

Perišić's career has been marked by his consistency and adaptability, playing in various positions and leagues. His success with Inter Milan and Bayern Munich has made him one of the most successful Croatian players of his generation.

Overall, Ivan Perišić is a highly skilled and decorated footballer who has made a significant impact in the world of football. His versatility, work rate, and goal-scoring ability have made him a valuable asset to his teams, and he continues to be an important player for both club and country.

title: Gemma Arterton
text:
Gemma Arterton is a British actress born on February 2, 1986, in Gravesend, Kent, with a condition called polydactyly, which resulted in extra fingers that were removed shortly after her birth. Her mother, Sally-Anne Heap, runs a cleaning business, and her father, Barry J. Arterton, is a welder. They divorced when Arterton was a young child, and she grew up on a council estate with her mother and younger sister, Hannah Arterton, who is also an actress. Her matrilineal great-grandmother was a German-Jewish concert violinist.

Arterton attended Gravesend Grammar School for Girls and made her amateur stage debut in a production of Alan Ayckbourn's The Boy Who Fell into a Book. She later studied at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, graduating in 2008. After her stage debut in Shakespeare's Love's Labour's Lost at the Globe Theatre in 2007, Arterton made her feature-film debut in the comedy St Trinian's (2007) as Head Girl Kelly.

Arterton gained recognition for her role as Bond Girl Strawberry Fields in the James Bond film Quantum of Solace (2008), which won her an Empire Award for Best Newcomer. She has since appeared in a number of films, including The Disappearance of Alice Creed (2009), Tamara Drewe (2010), Clash of the Titans (2010), Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time (2010), Hansel & Gretel: Witch Hunters (2013), Their Finest (2016), The Escape (2017), Vita and Virginia (2018), and Culprits (2023).

In addition to her film work, Arterton has also had a successful theatre career, with notable performances in The Duchess of Malfi (2014), Made in Dagenham (2014), Nell Gwynn (2016), and Saint Joan (2017). Her performance in Made in Dagenham earned her a nomination for an Olivier Award for Best Actress in a Musical, and she won the Evening Standard award for Newcomer in a Musical.

Arterton has been recognized for her contributions to the film industry, including being named as one of the 928 new members invited to join the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences in 2018. She has also been involved in several charitable initiatives, including the Time's Up and ERA 50:50 movements.

In 2016, Arterton set up her own production company, Rebel Park Productions, which focuses on creating female-led content in front of and behind the camera. She produced the short film Leading Lady Parts in support of Time's Up and has produced and starred in several projects, including The Escape, which earned her a nomination for a BIFA for Best Actress in a British Independent Film.

Arterton has received numerous awards and nominations for her performances, including the Harper's Bazaar Woman of the Year Award for her work on The Escape. She has also been nominated for several Olivier Awards and has won the Evening Standard Theatre Award.

In her personal life, Arterton married actor Rory Keenan in 2019, and they have a son born in December 2022. She has been open about her experiences with fame and her support for various charitable causes. With a career spanning over 15 years, Arterton has established herself as a talented and versatile actress, with a wide range of performances in film, theatre, and television.

title: Nuh Omar
text:
Nuh Omar is a director and screenwriter born on June 5, 1988, in Karachi, Pakistan, to the Indian/Pakistani Kureishi family. His family has a rich history, with his grandfather being entrepreneur Safdar Kureishi, and his relatives including notable figures such as Hanif Kureishi and Maki Kureishi. Nuh's mother was a pioneering sports photojournalist in Pakistan, and he has an older sister and a younger brother. He received his early education at Karachi Grammar School, where he was a classmate of Bilawal Bhutto Zardari.

Nuh pursued his passion for filmmaking by attending the New York Film Academy in 2006, where he participated in its first 2nd Year Film Program. He later graduated with a bachelor's degree in The Science of Film from Full Sail University. After completing his education, Nuh interned with Scott Gardenhour at The Institute and worked as a freelance assistant director on several award-winning short films and documentaries. He also wrote and produced the short film "We're Americans, Eh?", which won the Audience Award and the award for Best Wardrobe at the 24 Hour Film Festival in 2011.

In 2012, Nuh returned to Pakistan and collaborated with Y Productions and producer Ayesha Jalil on a series of short films for the Engro Corporation Excellence Awards. One of his notable works from this period is "Mojiza-e-Fun" (The Miracle of Art), a short film about sculptor Shahid Sajjad, which was the final project to feature Sajjad before his death. Nuh continued to work on various projects, including freelance writing and directing for internet-based platforms, and ghostwriting commercials.

In 2012, Nuh joined DeVida Lifestyle, an entertainment channel, as an in-house and promo director. He later worked at advertising agency IAL Saatchi & Saatchi, where he worked on global projects and brands such as Head & Shoulders, Safeguard, Pampers, and Commander Safeguard. In 2014, Nuh parted ways with the company to focus on filmmaking. He began directing and writing episodes for "The Fortress of Dorkness", a YouTube resource channel for pop culture movies and comics, which has produced over 100 episodes since 2015.

Nuh has worked on several projects, including "The Alexandrian", an episodic historical drama about Cleopatra, and "The Porter & The Stone", a modern adaptation of Oscar Wilde's "The Happy Prince", which has won numerous awards. His TV pilot screenplay, "A Matter of Time", co-written with Christian Villarreal, won the grand prize at Filmmatic's TV Pilot Awards Season 6. Nuh is currently working on several projects, including "The Universe at Midnight" and "Tijuana Bible", and is also writing two feature films, "The Imaginary Friend Society" and "Ophelia".

Nuh lives and works in Karachi, Pakistan, and Los Angeles, CA. He has been open about his struggles with depression and is an advocate for mental health awareness. Throughout his career, Nuh has demonstrated his versatility and creativity as a director and screenwriter, and his projects showcase his passion for storytelling and filmmaking.

title: Jeremy Corbyn
text:
Jeremy Corbyn is a British politician who has been a Member of Parliament (MP) for Islington North since 1983. Born on May 26, 1949, in Chippenham, Wiltshire, Corbyn joined the Labour Party as a teenager and became active in politics at a young age. He was educated at Adams Grammar School in Newport, Shropshire, and later worked as a reporter for a local newspaper and as a youth worker and geography teacher in Jamaica.

Corbyn's early life and politics were shaped by his parents, who were Labour Party members and peace campaigners. He became involved in the Labour Party Young Socialists and the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament while still at school. After completing his education, Corbyn worked as a trade union representative and was elected to Haringey Council in 1974. He became a key figure in the Labour Party's left wing, supporting the socialist Campaign Group and advocating for workers' rights.

In 1983, Corbyn was elected MP for Islington North, defeating the Independent Labour incumbent Michael O'Halloran. As a backbencher, he consistently voted against the Labour whip, including during the New Labour governments. Corbyn was a vocal opponent of the Iraq War and chaired the Stop the War Coalition from 2011 to 2015. He also campaigned for a united Ireland and Palestinian statehood, and was involved in various anti-apartheid and anti-fascist activities.

Corbyn's activism has been shaped by his commitment to socialism and his opposition to injustice. He has been involved in various campaigns, including the Anti-Apartheid Movement, the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, and the Stop the War Coalition. He has also been a vocal critic of the European Union, but supported the Remain campaign in the 2016 EU membership referendum.

In 2015, Corbyn won the Labour Party leadership election and became Leader of the Opposition. During his tenure, he advocated for renationalizing public utilities and railways, a less interventionist military policy, and reversing austerity cuts to welfare and public services. He also oversaw a significant increase in Labour Party membership.

Corbyn's leadership was marked by controversy, particularly surrounding antisemitism within the party. He condemned antisemitism and apologized for its presence, while also strengthening disciplinary procedures regarding hate speech and racism. In 2019, he endorsed holding a referendum on the withdrawal agreement, with a personal stance of neutrality.

In the 2019 general election, Labour's vote share fell to 32%, resulting in a loss of 60 seats. Corbyn remained Labour leader for four months while the leadership election to replace him took place. His resignation as Labour leader formally took effect in April 2020, following the election of Keir Starmer.

Corbyn was later suspended from the Labour Party in 2020 after making comments about antisemitism, and was subsequently expelled from the party in 2024. He went on to stand as an independent candidate in the 2024 general election, winning re-election with a majority of 7,247. In July 2025, Corbyn announced the formation of a new political party with fellow independent MP Zarah Sultana. Throughout his career, Corbyn has been a vocal advocate for social justice and human rights, and has been a prominent figure in British politics for over four decades.

title: Jackie Shroff
text:
Jackie Shroff, born Jaikishan Kakubhai Shroff on February 1, 1957, in Mumbai, Maharashtra, is a renowned Indian actor and former model who has been active in the film industry for over four decades. With a career spanning over 40 years, he has appeared in 250 films in 13 languages, primarily working in the Hindi film industry. Shroff's journey in the film industry began with an uncredited small appearance in Swami Dada (1982), followed by his lead debut with Subhash Ghai's blockbuster actioner Hero (1983), which catapulted him to overnight stardom.

Throughout his career, Shroff has established himself as a versatile actor, taking on various roles in top-grossing films. In the 1980s and 1990s, he appeared in a string of successful films, including Teri Meherbaniyan, Aaj Ka Daur, Karma, Ram Lakhan, Tridev, Baap Numbri Beta Dus Numbri, Izzat, Khalnayak, Rangeela, Agni Sakshi, Border, and Bandhan. His performances in Parinda (1989) earned him the Filmfare Award for Best Actor, while his roles in 1942: A Love Story and Rangeela earned him consecutive Filmfare Awards for Best Supporting Actor.

In the 2000s, Shroff transitioned to more supporting and negative roles in films like Refugee, Mission Kashmir, Devdas, Hulchul, Bhagam Bhag, Apna Sapna Money Money, Dhoom 3, Happy New Year, Housefull 3, Bharat, and Sooryavanshi. He has also worked in films of other languages, including Punjabi, Konkani, Tamil, and Telugu. Notably, he made his debut in Konkani with the film Soul Curry (2017), which earned him the Goa State Award for Best Actor.

Apart from his acting career, Shroff is also an environmentalist and has been involved in various social causes. He is married to model and producer Ayesha Dutt, with whom he has two children, actor Tiger Shroff and entrepreneur Krishna Shroff. The couple runs a media company, Jackie Shroff Entertainment Limited, and has been involved in various philanthropic endeavors, including supporting HIV/AIDS awareness and abolishing female foeticide.

Throughout his career, Shroff has received numerous accolades, including four Filmfare Awards. He has also been recognized for his contributions to Indian cinema, including the Special Honour Jury Award for outstanding contribution to Indian cinema and the Raj Kapoor Special Contribution Award. Shroff has also made appearances on television, hosting shows like Lehrein, Chirtrahar, and Missing, and has been a judge on the magic show India's Magic Star.

In recent years, Shroff has continued to work in films and television, making his digital debut with the series Criminal Justice in 2019. He has also been involved in various other projects, including the film Paltan (2018) and the upcoming film Housefull 5. With a career spanning over four decades, Jackie Shroff has established himself as one of the most respected and versatile actors in the Indian film industry.

title: Antonio Leviste
text:
Antonio Leviste, also known as Jose Antonio "Tony" Casals Leviste, is a Filipino politician and businessman born on January 16, 1940. He comes from a prominent family in Batangas, known for their achievements in business and politics. Leviste was married to Senator Loren Legarda, although they separated before the 2004 election campaign. He has a daughter, Toni Leviste, a renowned equestrian who has won numerous medals in the Asian Games.

Leviste's early life and education led him to become the president of the Student Varsitarian, a prestigious campus organization, during his time at the Lyceum of the Philippines, which he graduated from in 1959. He later served as the Governor of Batangas from 1972 to 1980, a position that allowed him to hold various other roles, including member of the Batasang Bayan, chairman of the Regional Development Council, and Vice President of the League of Governors and City Mayors.

As Governor, Leviste showed a commitment to environmental conservation, launching a forest ecosystem management program that has become a model for reforestation. This initiative earned him the "Ten Outstanding Young Men of the Philippines" (TOYM) award for Public Administration. He also received the "Realtor of the Year" award from the Business Writers Association of the Philippines.

In addition to his work in politics and environmental conservation, Leviste has held various leadership positions in government agencies and private companies. These include the People's Homesite and Housing Corporation, Philippine Ports Authority, Philippine Aerospace Development Corporation, Semirara Mining Corporation, and the Philippine Tourism Authority. He has also co-founded several organizations, including the Pasay Board of Realtors and the Philippine Association of Real Estate Boards.

However, Leviste's life took a dramatic turn in 2009 when he was convicted of homicide for the killing of his longtime friend and aide, Rafael de las Alas. Leviste admitted to the crime, claiming that he acted in self-defense. He was sentenced to six to twelve years in prison and served his sentence at the National Bilibid Prison in Muntinlupa.

Leviste was released from prison on December 6, 2013, after his parole was granted. Since his release, he has continued to be involved in various business and tourism-related activities. He is currently the charter president of the Resort Association of the Philippines and co-founder of the Tourism Council of the Philippines. Leviste is also the chief executive officer of the Leviste Group of Companies, a real estate firm engaged in housing, subdivision, condominium, and resort development.

title: Sami Shalom Chetrit
text:
Sami Shalom Chetrit is a Moroccan-born Hebrew poet, inter-disciplinary scholar, teacher, and Israeli social and peace activist. Born in 1960 in Errachidia, Morocco, Chetrit's family moved to Israel when he was three years old, and he grew up in Ashdod. He pursued his academic interests in literature and political science, earning a BA, MA, and PhD in political science from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, as well as an MA in International Affairs from Columbia University in New York.

Chetrit currently lives in New York City, where he teaches Hebrew language, literature, and culture, as well as Middle Eastern studies at Queens College in Flushing, New York. His activism and scholarly work focus on social justice, cultural freedom, and peace in Israel-Palestine. As a Mizrahi activist, he was one of the founders of Kedma, an alternative school system that advocated for equal opportunities and a multi-cultural curriculum. He also co-founded HaKeshet HaDemokratit HaMizrakhit, a coalition for social justice and cultural freedom.

In addition to his academic and activist work, Chetrit is a prolific writer and poet. He has authored numerous articles and books on culture, society, and politics in Israel, as well as a novel and four books of poetry. His published works include "Intra-Jewish Conflict in Israel: White Jews, Black Jews," a book that explores the complexities of Jewish identity in Israel. He has also produced two documentary films, including "The Black Panthers (in Israel) Speak," which examines the Israeli social-protest movement of the 1970s, and "Az'i Ayima (come mother)," a film about Moroccan women of the first generation in Israel.

Chetrit's work has been published in various literary magazines, journals, and anthologies, and he has received recognition for his contributions to Israeli literature and culture. He identifies as an Arab Jew and is the founder of a democratic Mizrahi blog that advocates for social justice and peace in Israel-Palestine. Through his writing, teaching, and activism, Chetrit seeks to promote a more nuanced understanding of Israeli society and culture, and to advance the cause of social justice and peace in the region.

Throughout his career, Chetrit has been committed to exploring the complexities of identity, culture, and politics in Israel and beyond. His work reflects a deep engagement with the social and cultural issues of his time, and a commitment to promoting greater understanding and empathy between different communities. As a poet, scholar, and activist, Chetrit continues to make important contributions to the literary and cultural landscape of Israel and the wider region.

Chetrit's publications include several books and articles on Israeli politics and society, as well as poetry collections such as "Yehudim" and "Shirim Beashdodit". His work has been widely praised for its insight and nuance, and he is recognized as one of the leading voices of his generation. Through his writing and activism, Chetrit continues to advocate for social justice, peace, and greater understanding between different communities in Israel and beyond.

title: Jeff Long (athletic director)
text:
Jeff Long is an American athletics director who has held various positions at several universities. Born on September 21, 1959, Long earned his bachelor's degree in economics from Ohio Wesleyan University in 1982 and his master's degree in education from Miami University in 1983. He began his career in administration at Eastern Kentucky University, and later held positions at Virginia Tech, University of Michigan, and University of Oklahoma.

In 2008, Long became the Vice Chancellor and director of athletics at the University of Arkansas, succeeding longtime athletic director Frank Broyles. During his tenure at Arkansas, Long made a notable hire in 2008, bringing in football coach Bobby Petrino. However, his time with Petrino was short-lived, as the coach was fired in April 2012 after it was discovered that he had been carrying on an extramarital affair with a former Arkansas volleyball player, Jessica Dorrell. Long was angered by Petrino's deception and the potential liability the situation posed to the university. The incident led to a tumultuous period for the football program, with the hiring of interim coach John L. Smith and eventually Bret Bielema.

In 2013, Long was announced as the first chairman of the College Football Playoff selection committee. However, his time at Arkansas was cut short when he was let go effective immediately in November 2017, with the school's chancellor citing a loss of support from fans, alumni, and key supporters.

Long joined the University of Kansas as athletic director in 2018, where he aimed to turn around the school's struggling football program. He fired coach David Beaty and hired former LSU coach Les Miles, a friend from his time at Michigan. However, Miles' tenure was marked by controversy, and he was eventually forced out due to a sexual harassment scandal dating back to his time at LSU. Long faced criticism for his handling of the situation, including his vetting process for Miles.

The controversy surrounding Miles ultimately led to Long's departure from Kansas. On March 9, 2021, Long announced that he was leaving KU, with Chancellor Douglas Girod stating that it was in the school's best interest for Long to step down. Long later confirmed that his departure was not entirely voluntary, and that he had been "relieved of his duties" but allowed to publicly save face by resigning.

In his personal life, Long is married to Fanny Gellrich, and they have two daughters. Throughout his career, Long has held various leadership positions in college athletics, including his role as chairman of the College Football Playoff selection committee. Despite his accomplishments, his time at Kansas and Arkansas was marked by controversy, ultimately leading to his departure from both institutions. Long's legacy as an athletic director is complex, with both notable successes and significant challenges. His experience at Kansas and Arkansas serves as a reminder of the complexities and difficulties of leadership in college athletics.

title: Sandra Pisani
text:
Sandra Pisani was a highly accomplished Australian field hockey player, selector, and coach who made significant contributions to the sport. Born on January 23, 1959, in Adelaide, South Australia, Pisani began playing A-grade club hockey for Burnside Hockey Club in 1976 at the age of 17. She went on to play in eight winning A-grade premiership teams over 15 years, including four premierships in five years. Pisani's impressive playing career included winning the Association Medal for South Australia's Best and Fairest Player in 1985 and 1992.

Pisani's international hockey career spanned from 1981 to 1988, during which she played 85 games for Australia and scored a bronze medal at the 1983 World Cup in Malaysia. She was also part of the team that won Australia's first Olympic gold medal at the 1988 Summer Olympics in Seoul. Pisani captained the Australian team from 1985 to 1987 and was a key player in the team's success during that period.

In addition to her playing career, Pisani was also involved in coaching and selection. She coached the Port Adelaide hockey team from 1991 to 1994, leading them to a premiership in 1993 and being awarded Hockey SA's Coach of the Year. Pisani was also a National Women's Senior Selector for the Hockeyroos Australia women's national field hockey team from 1993 to 2000, during which the team won two Olympic gold medals under coach Ric Charlesworth.

Pisani's contributions to hockey were recognized through various awards and honors. She was awarded the Medal of the Order of Australia (OAM) in 1989 for her service to the sport. In 2000, she was awarded the Australian Sports Medal for her contribution to Australian sport. Pisani was also inducted into the South Australian Sport Hall of Fame in 2015 and was a finalist in the Caltex SA Sports Star of the Year Award.

Throughout her life, Pisani was committed to the sport of hockey, holding various roles including state selector, state coach, and team manager. She was also a mentor and assistant coach for the Southern Suns and worked as a selector and manager for various Australian teams. Pisani passed away on April 19, 2022, after a battle with cancer, leaving behind a legacy of achievement and dedication to the sport of hockey. Her contributions to the sport continue to inspire and influence new generations of hockey players and administrators. Pisani's achievements serve as a testament to her hard work, dedication, and passion for the sport.

title: José Hernández Delgadillo
text:
José Hernández Delgadillo was a renowned Mexican painter and muralist who dedicated his life to creating art that reflected the struggles and injustices of his time. Born in 1927 in Tepeapulco, Hidalgo, Hernández Delgadillo grew up in a poor rural family and had to work from a young age to support his family. He began his artistic training in 1945, studying painting and architectural drawing at the workshop of Antonio Navarrete Tejero in Mexico City. To make ends meet, he created portraits, and after his first individual exhibition, he decided to pursue advanced training at the Escuela Nacional de Pintura, Escultura y Grabado "La Esmeralda" from 1955 to 1960.

During his time at La Esmeralda, Hernández Delgadillo met Pablo O'Higgins, who inspired him to continue the ideals of Mexican muralism. This encounter had a profound impact on his work, and he went on to create over 160 murals in Mexico and the United States, many of which contained strong political messages. His work was influenced by the Mexican muralism movement, and he was particularly drawn to the ideas of Diego Rivera, José Clemente Orozco, and David Alfaro Siqueiros.

Hernández Delgadillo's artistic style was characterized by its expressionistic and often monumental quality. He worked in a variety of mediums, including oil, acrylics, mixed media, print, and poster making, as well as sculpture. His murals often featured simple, basic colors, but also nuanced uses of color to express anger at social injustices. Justino Fernandez wrote that Hernández Delgadillo's works had a "definite sense of the monumental and certain underlying classicism combined with personal expressionism."

Throughout his career, Hernández Delgadillo was also actively involved in politics. He believed in the importance of popular organization and non-violent pressure against the government. He wrote a weekly column for the Excélsior newspaper from 1980 to 1983, which allowed him to present an alternate point of view. He also stood for the Partido Mexicano de Trabajadores in the 38th electoral district in 1985 and was a pre-candidate for president with the PRD in 1987.

Despite his prolific career, many of Hernández Delgadillo's murals are in urgent need of restoration, and some have been lost due to deterioration or destruction because of their political messages. In 2013, an effort was begun in Pachuca to rescue and restore his murals in the city, which include Contradicciones y lucha en Hidalgo and Por la democracia, el trabajo y la soberanía nacional.

Hernández Delgadillo's main recognition was membership in the Salón de la Plástica Mexicana, an honor society for Mexican artists. After his death in 2000, the Salón de la Plástica Mexicana established the José Hernández Delgadillo Prize in his honor. A retrospective of his work was held in 2009, and in 2008, a biography of the artist, Muros de Insomnio, was published. Despite his contributions to Mexican art, Hernández Delgadillo's work has become somewhat obscure, largely due to the unpopularity of his radical political ideas.

In the United States, Hernández Delgadillo created murals in California, including one in San Fernando in 1981 and several works for the agricultural school of the University of California, Davis, in 1989. His work continues to be celebrated for its commitment to social justice and its role in carrying on the traditions of Mexican muralism. Today, his legacy is being promoted by his home state of Hidalgo, which has made efforts to rescue and promote his life and work.

title: Neil Sinclair
text:
Neil Sinclair is a Northern Irish former professional boxer, born on February 23, 1974. He had a successful amateur career, winning a bronze medal representing Ireland at the 1992 Junior World Championships in Montreal, and a gold medal representing Northern Ireland at the 1994 Commonwealth Games in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. 

Sinclair turned professional in April 1995, with his first fight taking place at the Ulster Hall in Belfast, where he knocked out Marty Duke. He went on to have a notable professional career, winning the British welterweight title from 2001 to 2003. In 2007, Sinclair announced his retirement from boxing, but he decided to return to the sport just a couple of months later. 

In 2008, Sinclair challenged once for the EBU European Union title, but was unsuccessful. Two years later, in 2010, he challenged for the WBO welterweight title, but did not succeed. During his professional career, Sinclair also won the Irish light-middleweight title in May 2009, defeating Henry Coyle with a stoppage victory at the Odyssey Arena in Belfast.

Throughout his professional career, which spanned from 1995 to 2010, Sinclair demonstrated his skills and determination as a boxer. His achievements include holding the British welterweight title and competing for the WBO welterweight title. Sinclair's amateur success laid the foundation for his professional career, which was marked by several notable victories and title wins. 

Sinclair's boxing record and achievements are recorded with the Commonwealth Games Federation and BoxRec, a website that tracks professional boxing records. After retiring from professional boxing in 2010, Sinclair's legacy as a skilled boxer from Northern Ireland continues to be recognized.

title: Felipe (footballer, born 1977)
text:
Felipe Jorge Loureiro, commonly known as Felipe, is a Brazilian football coach and former player born on September 2, 1977, in Rio de Janeiro. He is currently the technical director of Vasco da Gama, a position he assumed in 2024. As a player, Felipe was a left-footed midfielder and left-back known for his exceptional playmaking skills, ball control, dribbling abilities, and vision for orchestrating offensive plays.

Felipe began his career at Vasco da Gama, joining the club's futsal team at the age of six and moving to the fields in 1990. He made his first-team debut in 1996 and scored his first senior goal in 1997. Felipe became a regular starter for Vasco, helping the team win several titles, including the Campeonato Brasileiro Série A in 1997 and 2000, the Copa Libertadores in 1998, and the Campeonato Carioca in 1998. In 1999, Vasco sold Felipe to Roma for $20 million, but the deal was complicated, and Felipe only received clearance to play for Vasco in September.

Felipe's career took him to several clubs, including Palmeiras, Atlético Mineiro, Galatasaray, Flamengo, Fluminense, and Al Sadd in Qatar. During his time at Al Sadd, he won several collective and individual accolades, including the Qatar Stars League and the Emir of Qatar Cup. Felipe also had a successful stint at Flamengo, helping the team win the Campeonato Carioca in 2004.

In addition to his club career, Felipe represented Brazil in several international matches, making his debut in 1998 and winning the Copa América in 2004. He featured in a total of seven matches for the national side.

After retiring from football in 2014, Felipe transitioned into coaching. He began his coaching career in 2016, taking over as head coach of Tigres do Brasil. However, he resigned after just a few months. Felipe then worked as a football coordinator for Ponte Preta and later became the head coach of Bangu. In 2022, he took over as head coach of Confiança, but resigned after just a few months.

In 2024, Felipe returned to Vasco da Gama as a technical director and was later named interim head coach for the remaining three matches of the season. He was again named interim head coach in 2025 after Fábio Carille was sacked. Throughout his career, Felipe has won numerous titles and individual awards, including the Copa do Brasil Player of the Year and the Campeonato Carioca Midfielder of the Year.

title: Chi Pu
text:
Chi Pu, born Nguyễn Thùy Chi on June 14, 1993, in Hanoi, Vietnam, is a Vietnamese actress and singer who has gained immense popularity in the entertainment industry. Her father is a member of the Vietnamese military, and her mother is an English teacher. Chi Pu rose to fame after being crowned Top 20 Miss Teen Vietnam in 2009. She then pursued a career in acting, landing leading roles in several television dramas and sitcoms, including Waterdrop, Happy Dream, and 5S Online.

In 2013, Chi Pu made her acting debut in the television drama Waterdrop, which was broadcast on Vietnam National Television. She then appeared in several other TV dramas, including Happy Dream and 5S Online. Her performances earned her recognition, and she became a teen idol. Chi Pu also produced and acted in her first short film, Under One Sky, which received a Golden Kite Award. She continued to appear in various films and TV dramas, including Thần tượng (The Talent), Chung cư ma (Hush), and Hương Ga (Rise).

In 2014, Chi Pu starred in the television drama Vẫn có em bên đời (You’re Always by my Side), which received high ratings and earned her an HTV Award for Most Favorite Television Drama Actress. She also produced and acted in her second short movie, My Sunshine, which supported the LGBT community. Chi Pu's performances in Yêu (Love) earned her nominations for Best Actress at the 2015 Golden Apricot Blossom Awards and Green Star Awards.

In addition to her acting career, Chi Pu is also a talented singer. She officially started her singing career in 2017 and has since released numerous songs, including "Fighting Fighting," "Stay with me," and "Ngày bồng bềnh." Her music has garnered attention from media outlets and fans, and she has performed at various events, including Viral Fest Asia 2016.

Chi Pu has also been recognized for her influence on social media. In 2020, she was honored among Forbes list of Asia Pacific's 100 most influential digital stars. She has also won several awards, including Face of The Year 2022 - Most Favorite Female Actress, ELLE Style Awards 2017 - Actress of The Year, and WebTV Asia Awards 2016 - Most Popular Online Drama.

Chi Pu is also known for her activism and philanthropic work. She has supported several campaigns, including "Về đi Vàng ơi" (Come home Golden), which aimed to end the theft, trade, and cruel actions of dogs. She has also advocated for funding heart surgeries for poor children and urged people to contribute funds to support flood victims in Central Vietnam.

In her personal life, Chi Pu has been involved in several brand partnerships, including Yamaha Janus, Dove Vietnam, and OPPO Cameraphone. She has also launched her own fashion collections with TheBlueTshirt and PUSW. Chi Pu has been a brand ambassador for several companies, including Panasonic Beauty and Heineken.

In 2023, Chi Pu participated in the fourth season of the Chinese reality show "Sisters Who Make Waves," where she competed with other contestants and finished with the sixth highest score. She also won two sub-categories, including the "Fan Favorite" award and the "Overcoming Challenges" award. Chi Pu's performance earned her a position as part of the 11-member girl group that will debut and be active in the Chinese entertainment industry after the show.

Overall, Chi Pu is a talented and influential Vietnamese actress and singer who has made a significant impact in the entertainment industry. Her dedication to her craft, her passion for activism, and her influence on social media have made her a beloved figure in Vietnam and beyond.

title: Paul Anka
text:
Paul Anka is a renowned Canadian and American singer, songwriter, and actor born on July 30, 1941, in Ottawa, Ontario, to parents of Lebanese Christian descent. His mother passed away when he was 18 years old. Anka began singing in the choir at St. Elias Antiochian Orthodox Cathedral and attended Fisher Park High School, where he was part of a vocal trio called the Bobby Soxers.

At 14, Anka recorded his first single, "I Confess." Two years later, he traveled to New York City with $100 given to him by his uncle and auditioned for Don Costa at ABC Records. Anka sang a verse he had written to a former babysitter, which became the song "Diana," bringing him stardom as it topped the Canadian and US music charts. "Diana" remains one of the best-selling singles by a Canadian recording artist.

Anka's early success led to him becoming one of the biggest teen idols of the time, with hits like "It's Time to Cry" and "(All of a Sudden) My Heart Sings." He toured Britain and Australia with Buddy Holly and wrote "It Doesn't Matter Anymore," which Holly recorded just before his death in 1959. Anka composed the theme for The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson and wrote the English lyrics to Frank Sinatra's signature song "My Way," originally a French song called "Comme d'habitude."

Throughout his career, Anka has written hits for other artists, including Tom Jones' "She's a Lady" and the theme for the film The Longest Day. He has also acted in various films and television shows, including Let's Rock, Girls Town, Look in Any Window, The Longest Day, and American Idol. Anka's collaborations include duets with Odia Coates, with whom he had several Top 20 hits, and Celine Dion.

In the 1970s, Anka experienced a chart comeback with the hit song "(You're) Having My Baby," which exposed him to a new generation of fans. He continued to release music throughout the 1980s and 1990s, including the album A Body of Work, which featured collaborations with artists like Celine Dion and Kenny G.

Anka has performed in various countries, including Italy, Finland, and Israel. He has been recognized for his contributions to music, including being appointed an Officer of the Order of Canada in 2004. In 2016, Anka was a contestant on The Masked Singer, finishing in seventh place.

In his personal life, Anka has been married four times: to Anne de Zogheb from 1963 to 2001, with whom he had a daughter, Amanda; to Anna Åberg from 2008 to 2010, with whom he had a son; and to Lisa Pemberton from 2016 to 2020. Anka became a naturalized citizen of the United States in 1990. He has been involved in various business ventures, including co-founding the holographic tech startup ARHT Media.

Throughout his career, Anka has been honored with numerous awards and accolades, including a star on Canada's Walk of Fame and a place in the Songwriters Hall of Fame. His legacy as a singer, songwriter, and actor continues to be celebrated by fans around the world.

title: Peter Gallagher
text:
Peter Gallagher is a renowned American actor born on August 19, 1955, in New York City. He is the youngest of three children to Mary Ann, a bacteriologist, and Thomas Francis Gallagher, Jr., an advertising executive. Gallagher's background is Irish Catholic, and he was raised in Armonk, New York. He graduated from Tufts University, where he was active in theater, and later studied acting at the William Esper Studio and with Mira Rostova.

Gallagher's career spans over four decades, with his first major film appearance in Steven Soderbergh's "sex, lies, and videotape" in 1989. He gained fame for his roles in films such as "The Player" (1992), "Bob Roberts" (1992), "Short Cuts" (1993), "While You Were Sleeping" (1995), "American Beauty" (1999), and "Mr. Deeds" (2002). He also made a name for himself in musical theatre, particularly with his role as Sky Masterson in the 1992 Broadway revival of "Guys and Dolls."

One of Gallagher's most notable roles was as Sandy Cohen in the Fox television series "The O.C." from 2003 to 2007. He also had recurring roles in TV shows such as "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit," "Californication," "Covert Affairs," and "Grace & Frankie." In addition to his acting career, Gallagher released an album titled "7 Days in Memphis" in 2005, which included a studio recording of his performance of "Don't Give Up On Me."

Gallagher has received several awards and nominations for his work, including the P.T. Barnum Award from Tufts University in 2005 and the "Light on the Hill" award in 2007. He has also been involved in various charity events, including hosting an annual award ceremony called "The Sandy Cohen Awards," which provides a scholarship to a law school student at UC Berkeley who wants to become a public defender.

In his personal life, Gallagher is married to Paula Harwood, and they have two children, James and Kathryn, who is an actress and singer. He has continued to work in film and television, appearing in shows such as "Zoey's Extraordinary Playlist," "Grey's Anatomy," and "Grace and Frankie." Gallagher is set to return to Broadway in 2024 in a new play based on the life of Delia Ephron, titled "Left on Tenth." Throughout his career, Gallagher has demonstrated his versatility as an actor, taking on a wide range of roles in film, television, and theater.

title: Joseph Kony
text:
Joseph Kony is a Ugandan militant and warlord who founded the Lord's Resistance Army (LRA), a terrorist group designated by the United Nations Peacekeepers, the European Union, and various governments, including the United Kingdom and the United States. Born in September 1961 in Odek, Northern Region, Uganda, Kony is a member of the Acholi people. His father was a farmer and lay catechist of the Catholic Church, and his mother was an Anglican and also a farmer. Kony was an altar boy until 1976 and dropped out of elementary school at the age of 15.

Kony's early life and experiences during the Ugandan Civil War and the subsequent insurgency against President Yoweri Museveni's government led him to become a rebel leader. He participated in the Holy Spirit Movement and later founded the LRA in 1987, aiming to create a Christian state based on dominion theology. The LRA has been responsible for numerous atrocities, including the abduction of children to become child soldiers and sex slaves, and the deaths of over 100,000 people.

Kony has been accused of ordering the abduction of children, and it is estimated that approximately 66,000 children became soldiers, and 2 million people were displaced internally from 1986 to 2009. The LRA's activities have been condemned by government entities, and Kony has been indicted by the International Criminal Court (ICC) for war crimes and crimes against humanity. He has been subject to an Interpol Red Notice since 2006.

The LRA's campaign of violence has spanned several countries, including Uganda, South Sudan, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and the Central African Republic. Kony has claimed to be a spirit medium and has proclaimed himself the spokesperson of God. He has also claimed to be visited by a multinational host of 13 spirits, including a Chinese phantom.

The Ugandan government and international community have made efforts to capture Kony, including a failed attempt by the Ugandan army in 2008. The United States has also provided financial and logistical assistance to the Ugandan government in the hunt for Kony. In 2010, US President Barack Obama signed the Lord's Resistance Army Disarmament and Northern Uganda Recovery Act, aimed at stopping Kony and the LRA.

In 2012, a documentary film called "Kony 2012" brought international attention to Kony's activities, and several countries, including the United States, offered rewards for information leading to his capture. However, by 2017, the LRA's membership had significantly decreased, and both the US and Ugandan governments ended their efforts to find Kony, stating that the LRA no longer posed a significant security risk to Uganda.

As of 2022, Kony is reported to be hiding in the Darfur region of Sudan, where he is allegedly giving orders to his remaining fighters. In April 2024, Kony was reportedly settled in a camp in the Central African Republic, but after the Wagner Group attacked his camp, he and his men fled towards Sudan.

Kony's ideology is a syncretic mix of mysticism, Acholi nationalism, and heterodox Christian fundamentalism. He claims to be fighting for the Ten Commandments and defended his actions, saying that they are not against human rights. Kony's actions have been widely condemned, and his legacy as a notorious warlord continues to impact the region.

The International Criminal Court has scheduled an in absentia hearing for Kony in 2024, where he will be represented by a court-appointed lawyer. Kony's case is a significant example of the challenges of prosecuting international crimes and the complexities of bringing warlords to justice.

title: Dascha Polanco
text:
Dascha Polanco is a Dominican actress born on December 3, 1982, in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. She moved to the United States at a young age and was raised in Sunset Park, Brooklyn, and Miami by her father, a mechanic, and mother, a cosmetologist. Polanco is the oldest of three children, with a brother and sister. She developed an interest in acting from an early age but initially doubted auditioning due to her weight. As a result, she pursued a bachelor's degree in psychology at Hunter College, becoming a first-generation college student.

After completing her degree, Polanco worked in the healthcare industry, intending to become a nurse. She was working in hospital administration at Montefiore Medical Center in the Bronx while studying nursing. However, she eventually gained the courage to pursue acting again and registered with an acting studio, BIH Studios in New York. It was there that she was signed by the talent agency Shirley Grant Management.

Polanco's early acting credits include minor parts in the television series Unforgettable and NYC 22. Her breakthrough role came in 2012 when she was cast as Dayanara "Daya" Diaz in the Netflix series Orange Is the New Black. Initially a recurring role, she was promoted to a series regular in June 2014 for the show's third season. During her time on Orange Is the New Black, Polanco's daughter portrayed a younger version of her character in the fifth season.

In addition to her work on Orange Is the New Black, Polanco has appeared in various films and television shows. She made her film debut in the independent film Gimme Shelter in 2013, followed by roles in The Cobbler and Joy. She also starred in the film The Perfect Match and had a recurring role in The Assassination of Gianni Versace: American Crime Story in 2018. Polanco's other notable roles include appearances in the Netflix series Russian Doll and When They See Us, as well as the film In the Heights, where she played the role of Cuca.

Polanco has also lent her voice to animation, voicing Ms. Camilla Torres in the animated series Karma's World from 2021 to 2022. title: Alfred Hitchcock
text:
Sir Alfred Joseph Hitchcock was a renowned English film director, widely regarded as one of the most influential figures in the history of cinema. Born on August 13, 1899, in Leytonstone, London, he was the second of three children to William Edgar Hitchcock, a greengrocer and poulterer, and Emma Jane Whelan. Hitchcock's early life was marked by discipline, with his parents being Roman Catholics of English and Irish ancestry. He developed a lifelong phobia of law enforcement after being sent to a police station with a note as a five-year-old boy.

Hitchcock was educated at St. Ignatius College, a Jesuit grammar school, where he developed an interest in geography and maps. He became fascinated with trains and timetables, which would later feature in many of his films. After completing his education, Hitchcock worked as a technical clerk and copywriter before joining the film industry in 1919 as a title card designer for Famous Players-Lasky, the production arm of Paramount Pictures.

Hitchcock quickly gained experience as a co-writer, art director, and production manager on numerous silent films. In 1925, he made his directorial debut with The Pleasure Garden, a British-German silent film. His breakthrough film was The Lodger: A Story of the London Fog (1927), a thriller that helped shape the genre and established him as a prominent director.

Throughout his career, Hitchcock was known for his innovative filmmaking techniques, including his use of suspense, misdirection, and camera angles. He became a naturalized American citizen in 1955 and went on to direct over 50 feature films, many of which are still widely watched and studied today. Some of his most notable films include Rebecca (1940), Suspicion (1941), Shadow of a Doubt (1943), Lifeboat (1944), Spellbound (1945), Notorious (1946), Rope (1948), Strangers on a Train (1951), Dial M for Murder (1954), Rear Window (1954), Vertigo (1958), North by Northwest (1959), Psycho (1960), The Birds (1963), and Marnie (1964).

Hitchcock's films often featured cameo appearances by himself, and he became as well-known as any of his actors. He also hosted and produced the television anthology Alfred Hitchcock Presents, which ran from 1955 to 1965. Throughout his career, Hitchcock received numerous awards and nominations, including 46 Academy Award nominations and six wins. He was knighted in 1979 and received the BAFTA Fellowship in 1971 and the AFI Life Achievement Award in 1979.

Hitchcock's personal life was marked by his marriage to Alma Reville, whom he met while working on Woman to Woman (1923). The couple had no children, and Hitchcock was known to have had a complex and sometimes tumultuous relationship with his mother. He died on April 29, 1980, at the age of 80, leaving behind a legacy as one of the greatest film directors of all time.

In his later years, Hitchcock's films continued to be critically acclaimed, with many considering them to be among the greatest of all time. In 2012, Vertigo was voted the greatest film ever made by the British Film Institute, and as of 2021, nine of his films have been selected for preservation in the United States National Film Registry. Hitchcock's influence on cinema continues to be felt, and his films remain widely popular and influential to this day.

title: Chris John (boxer)

title: Amelia Earhart
text:
Amelia Earhart was a renowned American aviation pioneer born on July 24, 1897, in Atchison, Kansas. She developed a passion for adventure at a young age and gained flying experience from her twenties. In 1928, Earhart became a celebrity after becoming the first female passenger to cross the Atlantic by airplane. This achievement catapulted her to international fame, and she went on to become the first woman to make a nonstop solo transatlantic flight in 1932, earning her the Distinguished Flying Cross.

Earhart was a trailblazer for women in aviation, setting numerous records and promoting commercial air travel. She was also a vocal advocate for women's rights and a member of the National Woman's Party, supporting the Equal Rights Amendment. In 1935, she became a visiting faculty member of Purdue University, advising on aeronautical engineering and counseling female students.

In 1937, Earhart attempted to become the first woman to circumnavigate the globe, flying a Lockheed Model 10-E Electra airplane with her navigator, Fred Noonan. They disappeared on July 2, 1937, near Howland Island in the Pacific Ocean, and despite extensive searches, their fate remains a mystery. Earhart was declared dead on January 5, 1939.

Throughout her life, Earhart was driven by a sense of adventure and a desire to push boundaries. As a child, she was nicknamed "Meeley" and "Millie" and was known for her tomboyish behavior, enjoying activities like climbing trees and hunting rats with a rifle. Her upbringing was unconventional, with her mother, Amy Earhart, encouraging her children to be independent and not conform to traditional feminine norms.

Earhart's early life was marked by frequent moves, with her family eventually settling in Des Moines, Iowa. She developed an interest in aviation after attending the Iowa State Fair in 1908, but it wasn't until 1920, when she took a flying lesson with instructor Neta Snook, that she became hooked on flying. Over the next few years, Earhart saved up for lessons, worked as a photographer and truck driver, and eventually bought her own plane, a Kinner Airster.

Earhart's flying career was marked by numerous achievements, including setting a world record for female pilots in 1922 and becoming the 16th woman in the United States to earn a pilot's license in 1923. She also worked as a social worker and teacher, and wrote best-selling books about her flying experiences. Earhart's legacy has endured, inspiring generations of women to pursue careers in aviation and beyond.

In the years following her disappearance, Earhart's legend has only grown, with numerous books, films, and documentaries chronicling her life and exploits. She has been inducted into the National Aviation Hall of Fame and the National Women's Hall of Fame, and has been honored with numerous memorials, including a US airmail stamp, an airport, and a bridge. Despite the mystery surrounding her disappearance, Earhart's legacy as a pioneering aviator and feminist icon continues to inspire people around the world.

title: Mamunul Islam
text:
