title: Grayston Burgess
text:
Grayston Burgess was a renowned English countertenor and conductor, born on April 7, 1932, in Cheriton, Kent. As a young boy, he was a chorister in the choir of Canterbury Cathedral during World War II, which likely had a profound impact on his musical development. He later attended Cheltenham College and won a choral scholarship to sing in the Choir of King's College, Cambridge, under the direction of Boris Ord.

Burgess's professional career began to take shape when he became a member of the Purcell Singers. In 1963, he formed the Purcell Consort of Voices, with which he performed and recorded numerous works. He also collaborated with other prominent ensembles, including the Studio der frühen Musik and the Musica Reservata Ensemble, directed by Michael Morrow and John Beckett.

As a performer, Burgess premiered several important compositions, including Michael Tippett's "Songs for Ariel." He also sang with various ensembles and taught singing at Ellerslie School in Malvern and later at Malvern College. One of his notable pupils was Wendy Nieper, a former member of the Swingle Singers.

In the 2000s, Burgess accepted an invitation to help form a local community choir to celebrate the Millennium. The choir's performance of Haydn's Creation led to its continuation as Choir 2000, which became a staple of the community and a source of inspiration for Burgess. He continued to work with the choir, directing and inspiring its members.

Throughout his career, Burgess was recognized for his contributions to music. In 2017, he was interviewed by the Daily Telegraph and referred to as a "veteran conductor and choir director." Although the article highlighted his work and the presence of women in British cathedral choirs, it did not mention his connection to the Campaign for the Traditional Cathedral Choir, a group that advocates for the exclusion of women and girls from cathedral and church choirs.

Burgess's discography includes several notable recordings, such as his solo performance as a countertenor on the Dowland LP and his work as a conductor with the Purcell Consort of Voices on the Music of Albert: Prince of Saxe, Coburg und Gotha, released by Decca/Australian Eloquence. He passed away on March 6, 2019, leaving behind a legacy as a talented performer, educator, and conductor.

title: Tom Coburn
text:
Tom Coburn was a physician and politician who served as a United States Senator from Oklahoma from 2005 to 2015. Born on March 14, 1948, in Casper, Wyoming, Coburn grew up in a family of modest means. His father was an optician and founder of Coburn Optical Industries. Coburn graduated with a B.S. in accounting from Oklahoma State University and later earned a medical degree from the University of Oklahoma Medical School.

After completing his medical training, Coburn opened a private medical practice in Muskogee, Oklahoma, where he served as an obstetrician and treated over 15,000 patients, delivering 4,000 babies. He was also a deacon in a Southern Baptist Church and a devoted family man with three daughters.

Coburn entered politics in 1994, when he was elected to the United States House of Representatives, defeating a Democratic incumbent in a heavily Democratic district. He served three terms in the House, earning a reputation as a fiscal and social conservative. During his time in the House, Coburn was a strong advocate for term limits, gun rights, and the death penalty, and he opposed same-sex marriage and embryonic stem cell research.

In 2004, Coburn ran for the United States Senate, winning the election and serving two terms. During his time in the Senate, Coburn continued to uphold his conservative values, earning the nickname "Dr. No" for his frequent use of technicalities to block federal spending bills. He was a strong advocate for fiscal responsibility and was critical of deficit spending and pork barrel projects.

Coburn was also known for his use of the Senate hold privilege, which allows a senator to block a bill from coming to the floor for a vote. He used this power to block several bills, including a veterans benefits bill and a bill intended to help end hostilities in Uganda.

In addition to his work in Congress, Coburn was involved in several controversies, including a sterilization controversy surrounding a procedure he performed on a 20-year-old woman in 1990. The woman alleged that Coburn did not have her consent for the procedure, while Coburn claimed that he had her oral consent. The lawsuit was ultimately dismissed, but the incident drew attention to Coburn's views on abortion and informed consent.

Coburn also made headlines for his opposition to the TV broadcast of the film Schindler's List, which he deemed too violent and explicit for a 7 p.m. time slot. He later apologized for his comments, acknowledging that he had expressed himself poorly.

Throughout his career, Coburn was driven by his commitment to his conservative values and his desire to make a positive impact on his community. He was a strong advocate for his constituents and worked tirelessly to promote fiscal responsibility and limited government.

After leaving Congress in 2015, Coburn worked as a senior fellow at the Manhattan Institute for Policy Research, where he focused on healthcare reform and regulatory reform. He also served as a senior advisor to Citizens for Self-Governance, a group that advocates for constitutional government.

Tom Coburn passed away on March 28, 2020, at the age of 72, leaving behind a legacy as a dedicated public servant and a champion of conservative values. His commitment to his principles and his constituents earned him respect from both his colleagues and his constituents, and his impact on Oklahoma and the nation will be felt for years to come.

title: David Oyite-Ojok
text:
David Oyite-Ojok was a Ugandan military officer who played a significant role in the country's history, particularly during the overthrow of Idi Amin in 1979. Born on April 15, 1940, in Lira District, Oyite-Ojok was an ethnic Lango who joined the Uganda Army in 1963. He rose through the ranks, becoming a junior army officer in the late 1960s and teaching a training course for officer cadets in Jinja in 1965.

By 1971, Oyite-Ojok had reached the rank of lieutenant colonel but had to flee Uganda after Idi Amin overthrew President Milton Obote in a coup. Oyite-Ojok joined the guerrilla army Obote was organizing in exile in Tanzania, where he gained a "legendary" reputation in Uganda. He took part in a rebel invasion of Uganda in 1972, which aimed to restore Obote to presidency, but the operation resulted in a major rebel defeat.

Oyite-Ojok assumed a key role in the grouping of military exiles who, with the backing of Tanzanian troops, led the counteroffensive that resulted in the overthrow of Amin in 1979. He served as field commander for Obote's private army, Kikosi Maalum, and was appointed head of a Uganda National Liberation Army (UNLA) battalion in March 1979. Oyite-Ojok proved to be tactically adept during this conflict, eventually rising to chief of staff for the entire UNLA.

After Amin's overthrow, Oyite-Ojok became a member of the Military Commission, a powerful sub-committee of the Uganda National Liberation Front (UNLF) that ruled the country. He amassed a great amount of wealth, particularly through coffee export, and became chairman of the Coffee Making Board. Oyite-Ojok fully backed Obote, who was preparing to return from exile, and ensured that the national army under his command was overwhelmingly made up of Northerners.

As chief of staff of the UNLA, Oyite-Ojok was supposed to stay neutral and above the political disputes, but instead, he backed Obote, leading to the removal of Yusuf Lule from the Presidency. Oyite-Ojok gained greater power when "figurehead president" Binaisa dismissed him as army chief in May 1980, but the Military Commission removed Binaisa from office, and Oyite-Ojok became one of the leaders of the Presidential Commission.

Oyite-Ojok organized a personal death squad, led by Captain Patrick Ageta, which murdered several political opponents of the chief of staff. He campaigned on behalf of Obote in the 1980 elections, using his status as "legendary commander" to rally northerners to his cause. The elections resulted in Obote's return to power, and Oyite-Ojok was confirmed as Army Chief of Staff.

As Army Chief of Staff, Oyite-Ojok was responsible for attempting to defeat the guerrilla armies of Yoweri Museveni's National Resistance Movement (NRA) and Andrew Kayiira's Uganda Freedom Movement (UFM). He proved effective against these groups, but his tactics were often brutal, resulting in the deaths of thousands of civilians. By 1983, the UNLA under Oyite-Ojok had effectively defeated the NRA and UFM, but tensions emerged in the military, particularly between the Langi and Acholi tribes.

Oyite-Ojok's life was cut short on December 2, 1983, when he died in a helicopter crash in Nakitoma Sub-county, part of Nakasongola District. The circumstances of his death are still disputed, with some claiming that the NRA shot down his helicopter and others alleging that Obote had arranged his death. Oyite-Ojok's legacy is complex, but he has been honored by Museveni's government as a national hero.

title: Thomas Piketty
text:
Thomas Piketty is a French economist and professor of economics at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences, Paris School of Economics, and Centennial Professor of Economics at the London School of Economics. His work focuses on public economics, particularly income and wealth inequality. Piketty's research has been widely acclaimed and has had a significant impact on the field of economics.

Born on May 7, 1971, in Clichy, a Parisian suburb, Piketty grew up in a family that had been involved with Trotskyist groups and the May 1968 protests in Paris. However, his parents had moved away from this political position before he was born. Piketty's interest in economics was sparked at a young age, and he earned a C-stream Baccalauréat before entering the École Normale Supérieure at 18, where he studied mathematics and economics.

Piketty's academic career began with a PhD from the London School of Economics and the École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales, which he completed at 22. His thesis on wealth redistribution won the French Economics Association's award for the best thesis of the year. After completing his PhD, Piketty taught at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and later joined the French National Centre for Scientific Research.

In 2000, Piketty became a professor at the École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales, and in 2006, he became the first head of the Paris School of Economics. He has also been a columnist for the French center-left-leaning newspaper Libération and has written op-eds for the left-leaning newspaper Le Monde.

Piketty's research has focused on wealth and income inequality, and his work has been widely acclaimed for its use of novel data sources, including tax records, to study the distribution of wealth and income. His book, Capital in the Twenty-First Century, published in 2013, argues that the rate of capital return in developed countries is persistently greater than the rate of economic growth, leading to increasing wealth inequality. The book proposes improving education systems and a global tax on wealth as potential solutions to address this issue.

Piketty's work has also explored the historical development of inequality in various societies. His book, Capital and Ideology, published in 2019, examines the ideological systems that have been used to justify inequality and argues that a higher standard of living has not come from the sacralization of property ownership, but from social protests.

In addition to his academic work, Piketty has been involved in politics, advising various politicians, including François Hollande and Benoît Hamon. He has also been a member of the Labour Party's Economic Advisory Committee and has written for various publications, including The New York Times.

Throughout his career, Piketty has received numerous awards and honors for his contributions to economics. He has been awarded the Yrjö Jahnsson Award, the British Academy Medal, and has been elected an international member of the American Philosophical Society.

Piketty's work has had a significant impact on the field of economics, and his ideas have been widely debated and discussed. His research has highlighted the need for policymakers to address wealth and income inequality, and his proposals for a global tax on wealth and a more progressive income tax have been influential in shaping the debate on these issues.

Overall, Thomas Piketty is a prominent economist and academic who has made significant contributions to our understanding of wealth and income inequality. His work has had a lasting impact on the field of economics and will continue to shape the debate on these issues for years to come.

title: Richard Kuklinski
text:
Richard Kuklinski, also known as the Iceman, was an American serial killer and leader of a New Jersey-based burglary ring. Born on April 11, 1935, in Jersey City, New Jersey, Kuklinski's early life was marked by violence and abuse. His father, Stanley, was a violent alcoholic who regularly beat Richard and his siblings. Richard's older brother, Florian, died at the age of 7 due to injuries sustained from one of their father's beatings. Kuklinski's mother, Anna, was also abusive, often beating him with household objects.

Kuklinski's criminal activities began in the mid-1960s, when he worked at a Manhattan film lab and made bootleg copies of popular films and pornographic tapes. He became associated with members of the Gambino crime family, including Roy DeMeo, through his pornography business. Kuklinski's crimes escalated to murder in 1980, when he killed 42-year-old George Malliband during a meeting to sell him tapes. Malliband's body was found in a 55-gallon drum near a chemical plant in Jersey City.

Over the next few years, Kuklinski committed several more murders, often targeting men he met through his burglary ring or pornography business. His victims included Paul Hoffman, a 51-year-old pharmacist who was killed in a rented garage; Gary Smith, a 37-year-old member of the burglary ring who was poisoned with cyanide; and Daniel Deppner, another member of the ring who was strangled. Kuklinski's methods were brutal and varied, including shooting, strangulation, and poisoning.

Kuklinski's crimes went undetected for several years, and he was able to maintain a façade of normalcy with his family and neighbors. He was married twice, first to Linda and then to Barbara, with whom he had three children. However, his behavior was erratic, and he was prone to fits of rage, during which he would become violent and abusive towards his family.

In 1986, an 18-month-long undercover operation led to Kuklinski's arrest. He was convicted of four murders and sentenced to life in prison. In 2003, he received an additional 30-year sentence after confessing to the 1980 murder of NYPD detective John B. Shields, although this was later found to be an incorrect identification.

Kuklinski claimed to have murdered hundreds of people, often in gruesome and elaborate ways. However, many of these claims have been disputed by law enforcement and experts, who estimate that he may have killed around 15 people. Despite this, Kuklinski's crimes and persona have been the subject of numerous documentaries, books, and films, including a 2012 feature film, The Iceman.

Throughout his imprisonment, Kuklinski gave interviews to writers, prosecutors, criminologists, and psychiatrists, detailing his crimes and claiming to have worked as a hitman for the Mafia. However, many of these claims have been met with skepticism, and Kuklinski's true motivations and actions remain a subject of debate.

Kuklinski's legacy as the Iceman has been cemented in true crime lore, and his crimes continue to fascinate and horrify people to this day. He died in prison on March 5, 2006, at the age of 70.

title: Krystyna Szczepańska
text:
Krystyna Szczepańska is a Polish stage and costume designer born on August 18, 1950, in Kraków. She is the second child of Piotr Szczepański, a lawyer, and Stanisława née Żółtańska, a teacher of Russian language. Her parents came from Berezhany and were both members of the Home Army. Krystyna has an elder sister, Alicja, who is a lawyer.

Szczepańska was married to director Andrzej Maj, with whom she had two daughters, Magdalena and Elizabeth. Magdalena is a costume and set designer who is active mostly in the advertising industry. Szczepańska emigrated to Vancouver.

Krystyna Szczepańska primarily designed sets and costumes for her husband's performances. Her work includes various TV plays, films, and theater productions. title: Adnan Sami

Adnan gained international recognition with his album "Kabhi to Nazar Milao" in 2000, which topped the Indipop charts for most of 2001 and 2002, selling 4 million copies in India alone.

Throughout his career, Adnan has won numerous international awards, including the Nigar Award, Bolan Academy Award, and Graduate Award. In addition to his music career, Adnan has made headlines for his personal life, including his marriages to actress Zeba Bakhtiar and Dubai-based Arab Sabah Galadari. He married Roya Sami Khan in 2010, and they have a daughter, Medina Sami Khan, born in 2017. Adnan became a naturalized Indian citizen in 2016, after previously holding Canadian citizenship.

Adnan has been open about his struggles with weight gain and health issues, losing 120 kilograms in 16 months through diet and exercise. He has also been involved in various philanthropic activities, including performing for a song for famine-hit Ethiopia and writing a song for India during the 2003 Cricket World Cup.

Throughout his career, Adnan has been recognized for his contributions to music, including being dubbed the "Sultan of Music" by the Indian media. Adnan continues to be a celebrated figure in the music industry, known for his incredible talent, versatility, and dedication to his craft.

title: Chris Cuomo
text:
Chris Cuomo is an American television journalist anchor currently working at NewsNation, based in New York City. He was born on August 9, 1970, in the New York City borough of Queens, to Mario Cuomo, the 52nd governor of New York, and Matilda Cuomo. Chris Cuomo is the younger brother of Andrew Cuomo, the 56th governor of New York. His parents were of Italian descent, and their heritage had a significant influence on his upbringing.

Cuomo's early life and education were marked by prestigious institutions. He attended Immaculate Conception School in Jamaica, Queens, and then The Albany Academy, a private university preparatory day school in Albany, New York. He went on to earn an undergraduate degree from Yale University and a Juris Doctor from the Fordham University School of Law in 1995. As a licensed attorney, Cuomo began his career in journalism, appearing on various networks, including CNBC, MSNBC, and CNN, to discuss social and political issues.

Cuomo's breakthrough in journalism came when he worked as a correspondent and political policy analyst for Fox News and Fox Broadcast Network's Fox Files. He covered a wide range of stories, focusing on controversial social issues. In 2006, he joined ABC News as a news anchor for Good Morning America, where he covered major events, including the war on terrorism, Hurricane Katrina, and the Virginia Tech shooting. His work on ABC News earned him multiple Emmy Award nominations, a News Emmy, a Polk Award, and a Peabody Award.

In 2013, Cuomo moved to CNN to co-host its morning show, New Day. He later hosted his own prime-time show, Cuomo Prime Time, from June 2018 to May 2021. During his time at CNN, Cuomo interviewed various newsmakers and covered major events, including the Haiti earthquake and child custody cases. However, his tenure at CNN ended abruptly in December 2021, when he was fired after reports emerged that he had assisted in the defense against sexual harassment allegations against his brother, Andrew Cuomo.

The allegations against Chris Cuomo included claims that he had used his media sources to uncover information about his brother's accusers and had helped formulate statements for Andrew Cuomo. An internal review by CNN found that Cuomo had indeed been involved in his brother's defense, leading to his termination. Cuomo's departure from CNN was followed by several conservative commentators defending him.

In February 2022, Cuomo revealed in a recorded interview that he had considered killing himself after his firing from CNN. He stated that he had "was going to kill everybody including myself" following his termination. This statement highlights the emotional toll that Cuomo's termination had on him.

After his departure from CNN, Cuomo joined Nexstar Media Group to host a new primetime program on NewsNation. The show, titled Cuomo, premiered on October 3, 2022, and aims to provide neutral and less partisan commentary. Cuomo has also started a podcast, The Chris Cuomo Project, which was launched on July 21, 2022.

Throughout his career, Cuomo has received numerous awards and nominations for his reporting, including multiple Emmy Awards, a Peabody Award, and a Polk Award. He has been recognized for his coverage of breaking news, business news, and legal news.

In his personal life, Cuomo is married to Cristina Greeven, a Gotham magazine editor, and they have three children together. He owns homes in Manhattan and Southampton, New York. In 2020, Cuomo contracted COVID-19 and has since spoken publicly about his experiences with long COVID. Cuomo has been open about his struggles with the virus and its lingering effects on his health.

Overall, Chris Cuomo's career has been marked by his extensive experience in journalism, his notable achievements, and his controversies. His departure from CNN and subsequent move to NewsNation have raised questions about the role of journalists in reporting on their personal connections. Despite the challenges he has faced, Cuomo remains a prominent figure in American journalism, with a new chapter in his career at NewsNation.

title: Rangi Te Kanawa

Born in New Zealand, Te Kanawa is the daughter of Diggeress Te Kanawa and the granddaughter of Dame Rangimarie Hetet, and is affiliated with the Ngāti Maniapoto iwi.

After completing her studies, Te Kanawa undertook a six-month internship at the Textile Conservation Centre, Hampton Court Palace, and also spent time at the British Museum. Her expertise in Māori textile conservation led to her appointment at the Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa (Te Papa), where she works as a conservator and researcher. 

At Te Papa, Te Kanawa has been collaborating with a GNS forensic scientist on a project called the 'Whakapapa of Paru' to identify the provenance of cloaks in Te Papa's archives. Her work has also involved weaving, and her own weaving pieces have been collected by Te Papa. Te Kanawa is a member of the New Zealand conservators of cultural materials association.

In recognition of her services to Māori art and heritage preservation, Te Kanawa was appointed a Member of the New Zealand Order of Merit in the 2023 King's Birthday and Coronation Honours. Her research and publications include a paper on the conservation of Māori textiles in Aotearoa New Zealand, and a PhD thesis on reconnecting taonga kākahu to tangata whenua. 

Te Kanawa's work has been featured in various media, including a film on conserving cloaks and an interview on the challenges of preserving different Māori textiles. Her contributions to the field of textile conservation have not only helped preserve Māori cultural heritage but have also shed light on the significance of preserving traditional practices and knowledge.

title: Mohamed Abdi Mohamed
text:
Mohamed Abdi Mohamed, also known as Gandhi, was a Somali geologist, anthropologist, historian, and politician who made significant contributions to his country and the international community. Born in 1949, Gandhi was a highly educated individual with a double Ph.D. in geology and history and civilization of antiquity. He was a professor, scholar, writer, and politician who served in various capacities, including as Somalia's Minister of Defense, President of Azania (Jubbaland), and Ambassador to Canada.

Gandhi's academic journey began in Somalia, where he excelled in school and was awarded a full scholarship to study in France. He attended Besançon University, where he earned a Bachelor's degree in geology in 1976, a Master's degree in geology in 1979, and a Ph.D. in applied geology in 1983. He later earned a second Ph.D. in history and civilization of antiquity in 1990. Gandhi's academic excellence and expertise in various fields led to his appointment as a professor at the University of Besançon, where he lectured and conducted research.

Gandhi's professional experience spanned multiple fields, including geology, anthropology, and politics. He worked as a consultant to various organizations, including UNESCO, Doctors Without Borders, and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). He was also a senior program advisor for UNDP Somalia and a research officer at the Institute of Development Research. Gandhi's expertise in Somali studies led to his co-founding of the French Association of Somali Studies and the European Association of Somali Studies.

Gandhi's political career began in 2009 when he was appointed Somalia's Minister of Defense by Prime Minister Omar Abdirashid Ali Sharmarke. He held the position until 2010, when he was succeeded. In 2011, Gandhi was appointed as the first President of Azania (Jubaland), a new autonomous region in southern Somalia. During his tenure, he prioritized the removal of Al Shabaab militants from the territory. Gandhi's presidency ended in 2013, when Ahmed Mohamed Islam was elected to the office.

In 2014, Gandhi was appointed Somalia's Ambassador to Canada, marking the first time in over two decades that Somalia had an ambassador to Canada. As Ambassador, Gandhi was responsible for heading the Somali federal government's reopened embassy in Ottawa, Ontario. Throughout his career, Gandhi published numerous books and articles on Somali studies, including a Somali translation of poems for a poetry anthology of African sub-Saharan Africa.

Gandhi was also an active participant in the Somali peace process and served as a lead consultant in mapping the Somali civil society. He chaired the Technical Committee at the Arta Somali Peace process in Djibouti and the Somali Peace and Reconciliation Conference held in Kenya. Gandhi's commitment to peace and reconciliation in Somalia earned him recognition and respect from the international community.

In 2021, Gandhi announced his candidacy for the Somali presidency, a move that demonstrated his continued commitment to serving his country. Unfortunately, Gandhi passed away on April 18, 2021, leaving behind a legacy of academic excellence, public service, and dedication to peace and development in Somalia. Throughout his life, Gandhi demonstrated a passion for learning, public service, and peacebuilding, inspiring future generations of Somalis and international leaders.

title: Jimmy Weldon

Weldon's career spanned over seven decades, beginning in 1946 as a disc jockey at KWCO radio station in Texas. Webster became an integral part of Weldon's presentations, and listeners would often request to talk to the character.

Two years later, they made their television debut on The Webster Webfoot Show, produced locally by WFAA-TV in Dallas, Texas. The show was a huge success, and Weldon and Webster became household names in the Dallas area. Weldon passed away on July 6, 2023, at the age of 99, at an assisted living residence in Paso Robles, California. His legacy as a pioneering television host, ventriloquist, and voice actor continues to be celebrated by fans of all ages. With a career spanning over 70 years, Weldon's contributions to the entertainment industry are undeniable, and his memory will live on through his body of work.

title: Griselda Blanco

Blanco's life was cut short on September 3, 2012, when she was shot and killed by an assassin on a motorcycle in Medellín, Colombia.

Blanco's legacy as a ruthless and cunning woman in the cocaine trade has endured, with many documentaries, series, films, and songs telling her story. He was later sent to Bangalore to study medicine but had to return after his father's death. He married Shobha Nagi Reddy, daughter of former Andhra Pradesh minister S. V. Subbareddy, who also became a renowned politician. The couple had three children: one son and two daughters, one of whom is Allagada MLA Akhila Priya Reddy. Tragedy struck the family when Shobha Nagi Reddy died in a car accident on April 24, 2014, while campaigning for the 2014 legislative elections.

Nagi Reddy began his political career in 1984, when he was elected president of the Rudravaram Cooperative Society. He went on to become a mandal president in Allagadda MPP from 1986 to 1990. In 1991, he stood as an MLA candidate for the opposition Telugu Desam Party in the by-election for the Allagadda constituency, which was left vacant by the death of his brother Bhuma Sekhar Reddy. Nagi Reddy won the election and went on to serve in the 11th, 12th, and 13th Lok Sabhas.

In 1996, Nagi Reddy challenged Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao for the TDP in the Nandyal Lok Sabha constituency election. Although he was narrowly defeated, he gained many supporters and considerable publicity. He later defeated Rangaiah Naidu to join the 11th Lok Sabha. Nagi Reddy was a member of various committees, including the finance and external affairs committees, transport and tourism committee, and energy committee.

Nagi Reddy was known for his stance on the Rayalaseema region, which he believed should be part of Telangana and not divided with Andhra Pradesh. He cited cultural and emotional ties to Telangana, as well as the region's history of droughts and poverty. In 2007, he stated that 90 percent of coastal Andhra Pradesh's arable land was being irrigated, compared with 45 percent in the rest of the region.

In 2008, Nagi Reddy and his wife resigned from the TDP and joined the Praja Rajyam Party (PRP) founded by Tollywood film actor Chiranjeevi. However, when Chiranjeevi decided to merge the PRP with the Indian National Congress, Nagi Reddy and his wife opposed the move and joined the YSR Congress Party. In 2016, Nagi Reddy and his daughter, Bhuma Akhila Priya, returned to the TDP.

Nagi Reddy died on March 12, 2017, at the age of 53, due to a massive heart attack at his home in Allagadda. He was recognized for his role in the construction of a rail line from Yerraguntla to Nandyal. Throughout his career, Nagi Reddy played a significant role in Andhra Pradesh politics, serving the people of his constituency and contributing to various committees in Parliament.

title: John Craven
text:
John Craven is a renowned English journalist and television presenter, best known for hosting popular BBC programmes such as Newsround, Countryfile, and Beat the Brain. Born on August 16, 1940, in Leeds, West Riding of Yorkshire, Craven was educated at Leeds Modern School. His early life was marked by challenges, including his father's experience as a prisoner of war in Japan for three years during World War II.

Craven began his career in print journalism, working as a junior reporter on the Harrogate Advertiser, before moving on to the Yorkshire Post and freelancing for national newspapers. He joined the BBC in Newcastle upon Tyne, working on local radio and television, and later relocated to Bristol in 1970. In 1972, Craven became the host of Newsround, a pioneering children's news programme that drew on the full resources of the BBC. He presented over 3,000 episodes of the programme until his departure in 1989.

During his time on Newsround, Craven became associated with children's television, presenting news items on other programmes such as Multi-Coloured Swap Shop and Saturday Superstore. He also went on to become the editor of Newsround. After leaving the programme, Craven began presenting Countryfile, a countryside news programme for the BBC. In 2015, he presented the BBC Two game show series Beat the Brain.

In addition to his television work, Craven has been involved in various charitable initiatives. He took part in Gareth Malone's All Star Choir in 2014, which released a cover version of the single "Wake Me Up" to raise money for the BBC's Children in Need charity. Craven is also one of nine presidents of the Young People's Trust for the Environment, vice-president of the Waterways Trust, and Patron of SPANA. In 2016, he was appointed President of Radio Horton, a charitable hospital radio station.

Craven has received numerous awards and honours for his contributions to broadcasting. He was elected a member of the Royal Television Society in 1996 and awarded the RTS Baird Medal in 2002. In 2000, he was awarded the OBE for services to rural and children's broadcasting. Craven is also a fellow of the Linnean Society of London and received a Special Award for Newsround at the British Academy Children's Awards in 2011.

In his personal life, Craven is married with two daughters and lives in Oxfordshire. He has expressed his passion for his work, stating that he had no intention of retiring, enjoying the work he does too much. With a career spanning over five decades, Craven has established himself as a respected and beloved figure in British broadcasting.

title: Ahn Jae-hyun
text:
Ahn Jae-hyun is a South Korean model and actor born on July 1, 1987. He began his entertainment career as a fashion model in 2009, appearing in runway shows, magazine editorials, and commercials. His early work as a model gained him recognition, and he started to appear in television shows and music videos. In 2011, he gained further recognition for his role as a delivery man in the cable variety show "Lee Soo-geun and Kim Byung-man's High Society."

Ahn's acting career took off in 2013 when he played the role of actress Jun Ji-hyun's younger brother in the hit drama "My Love from Another Star." This led to more acting offers, including a role in the police comedy "You're All Surrounded" and the webtoon film adaptation "Fashion King" in 2014. He also became the MC for Mnet's weekly music program "M Countdown" in the same year.

In 2015, Ahn played his first leading role as a vampire doctor in the drama "Blood," and appeared in the fantasy drama "Snow Lotus Flower" alongside Lee Ji-ah. He continued to take on leading roles in various dramas, including "Cinderella with Four Knights" in 2016, "Reunited Worlds" in 2017, "The Beauty Inside" in 2018, and "Love with Flaws" in 2019.

Ahn has also appeared in several music videos and has been a part of reality TV shows. In 2016, he joined the cast of the travel reality show "New Journey to the West," replacing Lee Seung-gi who enlisted in the army. He has also starred in the Chinese romance film "Perfect Imperfection" alongside Taiwanese actress Ady An.

In his personal life, Ahn was married to actress Koo Hye-sun from 2016 to 2019. The couple met while filming "Blood" in 2015 and got married in May 2016. However, they announced their separation in August 2019, and Ahn filed for divorce, which was later finalized.

In addition to his acting career, Ahn has also published a photo essay titled "List of Things to Remember" in 2022. He has also been involved in philanthropic work, donating 10 million won to help orphans who have suffered from the coronavirus.

Throughout his career, Ahn has demonstrated his versatility as an actor and model, taking on a wide range of roles in various dramas and films. His personal life has also been subject to media attention, particularly his marriage to Koo Hye-sun and their subsequent divorce.

title: Bobo Baldé
text:
Dianbobo "Bobo" Baldé is a former professional footballer who played as a defender. Born on October 5, 1975, in Marseille, France, Baldé began his career in 1995 at Marseille, but couldn't make a first-team breakthrough. He then played for several clubs, including Mulhouse, Cannes, and Toulouse, before joining Celtic in 2001. During his time at Celtic, Baldé became a regular player and made 232 appearances, scoring several goals, including one in the Scottish Cup final against Rangers. He won five League Titles, three Scottish Cups, and two Scottish League Cups with the club.

Baldé's success at Celtic earned him individual recognition, including the Celtic Player of the Year award in 2002-03, voted by 40,000 fans. He was also named SPL Player of the Month in April 2003. In European competitions, Baldé played in the UEFA Cup final against Porto in 2003, where Celtic lost 3-2. He received a red card in the 95th minute of that match. Throughout his career, Baldé has received several yellow and red cards, and was involved in a few incidents, including racial abuse from some fans.

In addition to his club career, Baldé has represented Guinea at the international level, earning 52 caps and scoring two goals. He played in several Africa Cup of Nations tournaments and the 2006 FIFA World Cup qualifiers. After leaving Celtic in 2009, Baldé played for Valenciennes and Arles-Avignon. In 2013, he returned to Celtic for a charity match, and later became a sports coordinator for the Guinea national team.

Baldé has also worked as a playing assistant manager at Gombertois, his former youth club, and was appointed manager of Guinea's national U20 team in 2019. His younger half-brother, Yasser, is also a professional footballer in France. Throughout his career, Baldé has spoken highly of his time at Celtic, describing it as a "great adventure" and expressing his happiness with the experience he gained at the club.

title: Chacho Gaytán
text:
Gonzalo "Chacho" Gaytán is a multifaceted Mexican musician, composer, producer, and conductor who has made significant contributions to the music industry. He is best known as the co-founder and keyboardist of the Mexican pop band Sentidos Opuestos, which he formed with Alessandra Rosaldo. Gaytán comes from a musical family, being the brother of actress and singer Bibi Gaytan and brother-in-law of actor and singer Eduardo Capetillo.

As a producer, Gaytán has achieved notable recognition, including a Latin Grammy nomination in 2000 for Best Latin Children's Album for "Ellas Cantan a Cri-Cri". He has also worked as a musical director, notably for the production of West Side Story, and has arranged, orchestrated, and conducted orchestras in Mexico, including a performance at The Palace of Fine Arts in Mexico City with the National Philharmonic Orchestra. Additionally, he has collaborated with Fernando de la Mora in a concert with the Campeche Philharmonic Orchestra.

Gaytán is also the founder of the Mexican jazz band Manzana Jazz Band, showcasing his versatility and range in the music industry. Furthermore, he is the director of Azteca Music, a TV network in Mexico, and co-founder, musical producer, and director of MYST. His work spans various genres, from pop to jazz and classical music.

Gaytán's discography includes the 2007 album "Un día después". Throughout his career, he has demonstrated his talent and expertise as a composer, producer, and musician, earning him a respected place in the Mexican music scene. With his diverse range of projects and collaborations, Gaytán continues to be a prominent figure in the industry.

title: Rory Tapner
text:
Rory Tapner is a British businessman with a long and distinguished career in finance. Born on September 30, 1959, he was educated at Radley College and later earned an LLB degree from King's College London in 1982. Tapner's professional journey began in 1983 when he joined UBS AG, which was then known as SG Warburg, and went on to hold various leadership positions within the company and its predecessor firms.

During his tenure at UBS AG, which spanned over 25 years, Tapner held several key roles, including Joint Head of UK Corporate Finance, Head of UK Capital Markets Team, Global Head of Equity Capital Markets, and Joint Global Head of Investment Banking. He also served as Chairman of Investment Banking and eventually rose to the position of Chairman and CEO of UBS Asia Pacific in 2004. As Chairman and CEO, he was also a member of the UBS Group Executive Board from 2006 until his departure in June 2009.

After leaving UBS AG, Tapner returned to the UK and was appointed CEO of Coutts, the wealth management division of Royal Bank of Scotland Group, in September 2010. He led the company for nearly five years before stepping down in February 2015, when he was succeeded by Alison Rose. During his time at Coutts, Tapner oversaw the company's operations as a key player in the wealth management sector.

In addition to his role at Coutts, Tapner has held various other leadership positions. He was appointed Chair of the Board at Brown Shipley Holdings Limited in June 2019 and later became Chairman of the Board of Directors of Quintet Private Bank, Brown Shipley's parent company, in May 2020. Tapner has also been involved in various charitable and educational institutions, serving as the Hon. Treasurer and Chairman of the Financial Committee of the Council of King's College London for nine years.

Tapner has also been involved in promoting British snowsports, serving as Chairman of GB Snowsport, the governing body of British snowsports. He is a Fellow of King's College, London, and has been involved in various fundraising campaigns, including the "World Questions; King's Answers" campaign. Tapner's personal life is also notable, with his eldest son, Freddie, being the founder of The London Musical Theatre Orchestra, and his younger daughter, Rosie, being a TV presenter and model. Throughout his career, Tapner has demonstrated his leadership skills and commitment to various organizations, making him a respected figure in the business and financial communities.

title: Rafael Nadal
text:
Rafael Nadal, also known as Rafa, is a Spanish former professional tennis player who is widely regarded as one of the greatest tennis players of all time. Born on June 3, 1986, in Manacor, Mallorca, Spain, Nadal began playing tennis at the age of three and turned professional in 2001 at the age of 14. His early life was marked by a strong passion for sports, particularly football, which he played with his friends on the streets of Manacor. However, with the encouragement of his uncle and coach, Toni Nadal, Nadal focused on tennis and quickly rose through the junior ranks.

Nadal's junior career was impressive, with him winning several titles, including the Spanish junior championships in 1997 and 1998. He also reached the final of the U14 Spanish championship at the age of 12, a feat that remains unmatched. In 1998, Nadal won the season-ending U12 Junior Masters at Stuttgart, beating future world No. 5 Kevin Anderson in the final. This success led to him being awarded a tennis scholarship in Barcelona, which he turned down in favor of continuing his tennis training in Mallorca.

In 2001, Nadal began playing in professional tournaments, and his breakthrough came in 2002 when he won his first ATP match, defeating Ramón Delgado at the ATP 250 event on his home island of Mallorca. This victory made him the ninth player in the Open Era to win an ATP match before the age of 16. Nadal's 2003 season was marked by several Challenger titles and a win over No. 7 Albert Costa at the Monte Carlo Masters. He also reached the third round of Wimbledon, becoming the youngest man to do so since Boris Becker in 1984.

In 2004, Nadal reached the final of the Auckland Open and the third round of the Australian Open. However, his year was cut short due to a stress fracture in his left ankle, which caused him to miss three months of play, including the French Open and Wimbledon. Despite this setback, Nadal helped Spain win the Davis Cup title, beating world No. 2 Andy Roddick on clay to help his nation clinch the title over the United States.

Nadal's 2005 season was a breakthrough year, with him winning his first major title at the French Open, defeating Mariano Puerta in the final. He also won several other titles, including the Torneo Conde de Godó in Barcelona and the Monte Carlo Masters. These victories raised his ranking to world No. 3 and made him one of the favorites at the French Open. Nadal's success continued throughout his career, with him winning 22 major titles, including a record 14 French Open titles, and holding the No. 1 ranking in the world for a record 209 weeks.

Throughout his career, Nadal was known for his dominant play on clay courts, with his 81 consecutive wins on clay constituting the longest single-surface win streak in the Open Era. He was also a key member of the Spanish national team, helping them win five Davis Cup titles and two Olympic gold medals. Nadal's playing style was characterized by his powerful forehand, which he delivered with heavy topspin, and his ability to adapt to different surfaces.

In addition to his on-court success, Nadal has been recognized for his philanthropic work, particularly in his hometown of Mallorca. He has also been named one of the 100 most influential people in the world by Time magazine. Nadal retired from professional tennis in 2024, after playing for Spain in the Davis Cup Finals. His legacy as one of the greatest tennis players of all time continues to inspire a new generation of tennis players and fans around the world.

Nadal's achievements extend beyond his on-court success, with him being a role model for young tennis players and a symbol of Spanish tennis. His dedication to his sport and his philanthropic work have made him a beloved figure around the world. Nadal's story is an inspiration to anyone who has ever dreamed of achieving greatness in their chosen field, and his legacy will continue to be felt for generations to come.

title: Flávio Rocha
text:
Flávio Gurgel Rocha is a Brazilian businessman and former politician, born on February 14, 1958. He is currently the CEO and Chairman of Lojas Riachuelo, a major retail company in Brazil, as well as the CEO of its financial services subsidiary, Midway Financeira. The group also owns Confecções Guararapes, an industrial company, and Transportadora Casa Verde, a logistics subsidiary. Under his leadership, Riachuelo has grown to become one of the largest employers in the country, with over 40,000 employees as of 2017.

In addition to his business career, Rocha has also been involved in politics. In 1986, he was elected as a federal deputy for Rio Grande do Norte, representing the National Reconstruction Party (PRN). He was re-elected in 1990 for the Liberal Party (PL). In 1994, he attempted to run for the presidency but later supported the winning party, the PSDB, led by Fernando Henrique Cardoso. Rocha served as a federal deputy from 1987 to 1995.

Rocha's political views are centered around economic liberalism and a smaller government. He believes that the free market is a natural vehicle to fight corruption and advocates for a more efficient government. He has been a vocal supporter of conservative social values and has received recognition for his entrepreneurial achievements, including the Entrepreneur of the Year award from Isto É Dinheiro magazine in 2016.

In 2018, Rocha launched the "Brasil 200" manifesto, which promotes a liberal economic agenda and conservative social values. The manifesto was named in reference to Brazil's 200 years of independence. Rocha has also been an outspoken supporter of various political causes, including the impeachment of former President Dilma Rousseff and the candidacy of João Doria as mayor of São Paulo.

On a personal note, Rocha is a member of the neo-Pentecostal church Comunidade Evangélica Sara Nossa Terra, to which he and his wife belong. Overall, Flávio Rocha is a prominent figure in Brazilian business and politics, known for his advocacy of economic liberalism and conservative social values.

title: Bastian Schweinsteiger
text:
Bastian Schweinsteiger is a German former professional footballer who played as a midfielder. He was born on August 1, 1984, and is considered one of the greatest players Germany has ever produced. Schweinsteiger spent 17 seasons at Bayern Munich, playing in 500 matches across all competitions and scoring 68 goals. During his time at Bayern, he won numerous honors, including eight Bundesliga titles, seven DFB-Pokal titles, a UEFA Champions League title, a FIFA Club World Cup title, and a UEFA Super Cup title.

Schweinsteiger began his career as a youth team player at Bayern Munich in 1998. He quickly rose through the club's youth sides and made his professional debut in 2002 at the age of 18. Initially, he played as a left-back but later switched to a central midfield role. In 2002-03, he helped Bayern win a league and cup double, and he scored his first Bayern goal against VfL Wolfsburg in 2003.

Over the next decade, Schweinsteiger established himself as a key player for Bayern, making 135 appearances in all competitions and scoring 10 goals. He scored his first Champions League goal in 2004 and helped Bayern win the Bundesliga title in 2005. In 2008, he scored the first Bundesliga goal of the season, and in 2010, he extended his contract with Bayern until 2016.

Schweinsteiger's performances earned him recognition, and he was named the 2013 German player of the year. He was described by manager Jupp Heynckes as the best midfielder in the world. In 2012, he scored a crucial penalty kick against Real Madrid, but Bayern lost the Champions League Final to Chelsea.

In 2015, Schweinsteiger transferred to Manchester United, but he struggled to make an impact, playing sparingly for 18 months. He was eventually allowed to join Chicago Fire in 2017, where he helped the team qualify for the playoffs and was voted into the MLS All-Star Fan XI.

Schweinsteiger also had a successful international career, playing for Germany from 2004 to 2016. He earned 121 caps and scored 24 goals, helping Germany win the 2014 FIFA World Cup. He was instrumental in Germany's campaign, playing a key role in defending Lionel Messi in the final.

During his international career, Schweinsteiger participated in four European Championships and three World Cups. He scored his first two international goals against Russia and Tunisia in 2005. In the 2006 FIFA World Cup, he scored two long-range strikes against Portugal, earning him the Man of the Match award.

Schweinsteiger continued to play for Germany, participating in Euro 2008, the 2010 FIFA World Cup, and Euro 2012. He was named captain of the national team in 2014 and led Germany to victory in the World Cup. He retired from international football in 2016, after which he announced his retirement from professional football in 2019.

Since his retirement, Schweinsteiger has worked as an on-air football analyst for German television broadcaster ARD. He has also been involved in various charity initiatives and has been praised for his dedication to the sport. Throughout his career, Schweinsteiger was known for his exceptional skills on the field, and his passion and commitment to the sport have made him a beloved figure in the football world.

title: Maya Yoshida
text:
Maya Yoshida is a Japanese professional footballer who was born on August 24, 1988, in Nagasaki, Japan. He began playing football at a young age and joined Nagoya Grampus's U-15 team, where he was converted from a defensive midfielder to a centre-back. Yoshida made his professional debut for Nagoya Grampus in 2007 and quickly became a regular player, helping the team finish third in the league in 2008. He spent five seasons with Nagoya Grampus, making 124 appearances and scoring 15 goals.

In December 2009, Yoshida transferred to Dutch club VVV-Venlo, signing a three-year contract. However, his start to the club was delayed due to a foot injury, and he made his debut in October 2010. Yoshida quickly established himself as a regular player for VVV-Venlo, helping the team retain their Eredivisie league status. He made 24 appearances in the 2010-11 season and scored no goals.

In August 2012, Yoshida joined Premier League side Southampton on a three-year contract for a fee of around £3 million. He made his debut for the club in September 2012 and quickly became a regular player, forming a partnership with José Fonte. Yoshida helped Southampton avoid relegation in his first season and went on to make 34 appearances in all competitions. In the 2013-14 season, Yoshida's first-team opportunities were limited, but he made 14 appearances and scored two goals.

Yoshida regained his first-team place in the 2014-15 season, playing in the centre-back position, and helped Southampton finish seventh in the league. He made 23 appearances and scored one goal in the 2014-15 season. In the 2015-16 season, Yoshida started the season well, helping the club keep three consecutive clean sheets. However, he became a backup in the club's centre-back position and mostly appeared from the substitute bench.

In 2016, Yoshida started all six matches in the UEFA Europa League and helped Southampton reach the EFL Cup final. He captained the team for the first time in January 2017 and scored his first goal of the season in a 2-2 draw against Norwich City. Yoshida made a total of 27 appearances and scored two goals in the 2015-16 season.

In 2018, Yoshida joined LA Galaxy, becoming the new captain of the team. Throughout his career, Yoshida has also played for the Japan national team, making over 120 appearances and participating in several international tournaments, including the FIFA World Cup and the AFC Asian Cup. He was part of Japan's squad that won the 2011 AFC Asian Cup and finished as runner-up in 2019.

Yoshida's experience and leadership qualities have made him an important player for both his club and country. He has played in various positions, including centre-back, left-back, and right-back, and has been praised for his defensive skills and ability to read the game. With his move to LA Galaxy, Yoshida looks set to continue his successful career in Major League Soccer.

title: Erich Hartmann
text:
Erich Hartmann was a German fighter pilot during World War II, widely regarded as the most successful fighter ace in the history of aerial warfare. Born on April 19, 1922, in Weissach, Württemberg, Hartmann came from a family that valued flying, with his mother being one of the first female glider pilots in Germany. He began his flying career as a glider pilot at the age of 14 and gained his pilot's license in 1937. Hartmann joined the Luftwaffe in 1940 and completed his fighter pilot training in 1942.

Hartmann was assigned to Jagdgeschwader 52 (JG 52) on the Eastern Front, where he quickly made a name for himself as a skilled pilot. Under the guidance of experienced pilots, including Oberfeldwebel Edmund "Paule" Roßmann, Hartmann developed his tactics, including the "See – Decide – Attack – Break" approach. He flew his first combat mission on October 14, 1942, but it was not until November 22, 1942, that he claimed his first victory, an Ilyushin Il-2 Sturmovik.

Throughout 1943, Hartmann's skills continued to improve, and he became an "ace-in-a-day" multiple times, claiming five victories on several occasions. By the end of 1943, his tally had more than doubled, and he had become one of the top-scoring pilots in JG 52. Hartmann's success was not without its challenges, however. He was forced to crash-land his fighter 16 times due to mechanical failure or damage from enemy aircraft, but he was never shot down by direct enemy action.

Hartmann's achievements were recognized with numerous awards, including the Knight's Cross of the Iron Cross with Oak Leaves, Swords, and Diamonds. He was awarded the Knight's Cross on October 29, 1943, for destroying 148 enemy aircraft, and the Oak Leaves on March 2, 1944, for destroying 202 enemy aircraft. He received the Swords on July 3, 1944, for shooting down 268 enemy aircraft, and the Diamonds on August 25, 1944, for 301 aerial victories.

By the end of the war, Hartmann had flown 1,404 combat missions and participated in aerial combat on 825 separate occasions. He was credited with shooting down a total of 352 Allied aircraft, 345 Soviet and 7 American. Hartmann's last victory came on May 8, 1945, just hours before the German surrender.

After the war, Hartmann was tried and convicted of war crimes by the Soviet Union and spent 10 years in Soviet prison camps and gulags. He was released in 1955 and later joined the West German Air Force, becoming the first Geschwaderkommodore of Jagdgeschwader 71 "Richthofen". Hartmann was forced into retirement in 1970 due to his opposition to the procurement of the F-104 Starfighter. He went on to become a civilian flight instructor and passed away on September 20, 1993, at the age of 71.

In 1997, the Russian Federation posthumously cleared Hartmann of all charges, and his legacy as one of the greatest fighter aces in history has been cemented. Throughout his career, Hartmann was known for his exceptional flying skills, tactical innovations, and bravery in combat. His story serves as an inspiration to pilots and historians alike, and his achievements continue to be celebrated to this day.

title: John Forbes Nash Jr.
text:
John Forbes Nash Jr. was a renowned American mathematician who made significant contributions to various fields, including game theory, real algebraic geometry, differential geometry, and partial differential equations. Born on June 13, 1928, in Bluefield, West Virginia, Nash grew up in a family that valued education, with his parents encouraging his interest in mathematics from an early age. He was a child prodigy who learned advanced mathematics through books provided by his parents and grandparents.

Nash pursued his higher education at Carnegie Institute of Technology, where he initially majored in chemical engineering before switching to mathematics. He then attended Princeton University, where he earned his Ph.D. in 1950 with a dissertation on noncooperative games. During his graduate studies, Nash introduced several concepts, including the Nash equilibrium and the Nash bargaining solution, which are now fundamental to game theory.

Nash's work on game theory led to his receipt of the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 1994, along with John Harsanyi and Reinhard Selten. His contributions to game theory have had a lasting impact on the field, and his work continues to influence economics and other sciences.

In addition to his work in game theory, Nash made significant contributions to real algebraic geometry, differential geometry, and partial differential equations. He proved the Nash embedding theorems, which showed that any Riemannian manifold can be isometrically embedded in a Euclidean space. This work, recognized as one of the main achievements of 20th-century mathematics, has far-reaching implications for various fields, including physics and engineering.

Nash's work on partial differential equations, particularly his proof of the De Giorgi–Nash theorem, resolved Hilbert's nineteenth problem on the smoothness of solutions to elliptic and parabolic equations. This achievement earned him the Abel Prize in 2015, along with Louis Nirenberg.

Despite his impressive contributions to mathematics, Nash's life was marred by struggles with mental illness. In 1959, he began showing signs of paranoia and erratic behavior, which led to several years of treatment in psychiatric hospitals. His condition improved in the 1980s, allowing him to return to academic work.

Nash's life story was immortalized in Sylvia Nasar's biographical book "A Beautiful Mind" and a film of the same name, directed by Ron Howard. The film, which starred Russell Crowe as Nash, brought attention to his remarkable story and the challenges he faced.

Throughout his career, Nash received numerous awards and honors for his contributions to mathematics. He was a fellow of the American Mathematical Society and received the Leroy P. Steele Prize for Seminal Contribution to Research. Nash's legacy continues to inspire mathematicians and scientists, and his work remains a testament to the power of human ingenuity and perseverance.

Nash passed away on May 23, 2015, leaving behind a legacy of groundbreaking contributions to mathematics and a story of resilience in the face of adversity. His work continues to influence mathematics and science, and his story serves as an inspiration to future generations of mathematicians and scientists.

title: Noel Malicdem
text:
Noel Malicdem is a Filipino professional darts player who competes in events organized by the Professional Darts Corporation (PDC). Born on January 10, 1977, Malicdem has made a name for himself in the darts world, particularly in the World Championship. He first qualified for the World Championship in 2019, where he had a remarkable run, defeating Jeffrey de Graaf in the first round with a score of 2-3. However, his journey was cut short in the second round when he lost to Kyle Anderson with a score of 1-3.

Malicdem's success in the 2019 World Championship earned him a spot in the 2020 edition, where he qualified as a fourth-place finisher on the Asian Tour. In the first round, he convincingly won 3-0 against Rowby-John Rodriguez. His second-round match against Peter Wright was a closely contested one, with Malicdem leading and having match darts, but ultimately losing in a sudden-death leg with a score of 2-3.

Apart from his World Championship appearances, Malicdem has also represented the Philippines in the PDC World Cup of Darts. In 2019, he partnered with Lourence Ilagan to compete against England in the first round, but they lost and were eliminated from the tournament.

Throughout his career, Malicdem has shown his skills and resilience in the face of tough competition. His performance in the World Championship has been steadily improving, with a second-round finish in both 2019 and 2020. His achievements are a testament to his dedication and hard work, and he continues to be a prominent figure in the PDC darts scene.

Malicdem's statistics and profile are available on Darts Database, a reliable source for darts enthusiasts and fans. With his impressive performances and growing experience, Noel Malicdem is expected to make a lasting impact in the world of professional darts.

title: Zewde Gebre-Sellassie
text:
Dejazmatch Zewde Gebre-Sellassie was a prominent Ethiopian nobleman, historian, and politician who played a significant role in his country's government. Born on October 12, 1926, in the village of Galdu, northwest of Addis Ababa, Zewde was the son of Dejazmatch Gebre Selassie Baria Gabr, the governor of Adwa, and Leult Wolete Israel Seyoum. His family was of noble descent, with his grandfather being Ras Seyum Mengesha. Zewde's early education was in Addis Ababa, under a tutor, before he went to school in Jerusalem and Cairo, where his mother had moved during the Fascist occupation of Ethiopia.

After the liberation of Ethiopia, Zewde enrolled in the Haile Selassie I secondary school in Addis Ababa and later attended the University of Exeter in England, where he studied English literature. He then pursued legal training at St. Anthony's College, Oxford, becoming a senior member of the college from 1963 to 1971. During his time at Oxford, Zewde was called to the Bar, Lincoln's Inn, London. He later returned to Oxford to earn his PhD in the composite field of history, politics, and economics.

Zewde's career in government began in the early 1950s, when he held various offices under the imperial government, including economic attache, Head of Press, Information and Administration Division, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Director-General of Maritime Affairs. He rose through the ranks, becoming deputy prime minister, mayor and governor of Addis Ababa, ambassador to Somalia, minister of justice, and minister of foreign affairs. Zewde also served as permanent representative to the United Nations from 1972 to 1974.

However, in 1974, the Provisional Military Administrative Council, also known as the Derg, seized power and executed many high-ranking government officials, forcing Zewde to go into exile. He eventually became vice-president of the United Nations Economic and Social Council and worked as an advisor to the secretariat of the United Nations. Throughout his service, Zewde received national honors from at least seven sovereign states, including the Federal Republic of Germany.

In addition to his government career, Zewde was a prolific writer and published several books, including "Yohannes IV of Ethiopia: A Political Biography" and "The Conflict of Ethiopia and Eritrea: Causes and Solutions". He also wrote "The Blue Nile and its Basins: An Issue of International Concern" and "The Process of Re-unification of the Ethiopian Empire, 1868-1889". Zewde attempted to mediate between Ethiopia and Eritrea in 1998, along with other prominent Ethiopians.

Zewde was married to Woizero Alem Tsehai Araya and had a sister, Leult Ijigayehou Asfa Wossen. He passed away on December 15, 2008, leaving behind a legacy as a dedicated public servant, historian, and diplomat. Throughout his life, Zewde demonstrated a commitment to serving his country and promoting international understanding, and his contributions continue to be recognized and appreciated.

title: Ezechiel N'Douassel
text:
Ezechiel Aliadjim N'Douassel is a Chadian professional footballer who plays as a striker for Indonesian Championship club Bekasi City. Born on April 22, 1988, N'Douassel began his career in 2006 at local side Tourbillon in Chad. He moved to Algeria in 2007 to play for MC Oran and later joined USM Blida. During his time at USM Blida, he scored a brace against MC El Eulma in his debut, and went on to score five goals in 15 appearances. His performances caught the attention of European clubs, including Olympique de Marseille, Arsenal, Monaco, and Mallorca.

In 2009, N'Douassel was set to join Belgian club FCV Dender on a free transfer, but the move was not finalized due to contractual issues with USM Blida. He eventually joined Tunisian side Club Africain in 2011, where he played for several seasons and participated in the CAF Confederation Cup. In 2014, he was loaned to Paris FC, but the move fell through due to financial constraints. N'Douassel has also played for Israeli clubs Ironi Kiryat Shmona and Hapoel Tel Aviv, as well as Indonesian clubs Persib Bandung and Bhayangkara.

N'Douassel has been a key player for Persib Bandung, scoring 17 goals in the 2018 season and helping the team win several matches. He also played for Bhayangkara, scoring his first goal for the club in a pre-season cup game against Petaling Jaya City. In 2021, he scored a brace in Bhayangkara's first league match, earning them a 2-1 win over Persiraja Banda Aceh.

In addition to his club career, N'Douassel has also represented the Chad national team, making his debut in 2005. He is the national team's most capped player and top scorer, having played in various international tournaments, including the Africa Cup of Nations qualification and World Cup qualification. Throughout his career, N'Douassel has demonstrated his skills as a striker, scoring crucial goals for his teams and earning individual honors, including Liga 2 Player of the Half Season and Liga 2 Player of the Month awards. Currently, he plays for Bekasi City in the Indonesian Championship.

title: Lupe Vélez
text:
María Guadalupe "Lupe" Villalobos Vélez was a Mexican actress, singer, and dancer who made a name for herself during the Golden Age of Hollywood cinema. Born on July 18, 1908, in San Luis Potosí, Mexico, she was one of five children to a prominent family. Her father was a colonel in the armed forces of the dictator Porfirio Diaz, and her mother was an opera or vaudeville singer. Lupe learned to speak English and dance at Our Lady of the Lake in San Antonio, Texas, where she was sent to study at the age of 13.

Lupe began her career in Mexican revues in the early 1920s, performing under her paternal surname, Villalobos, until her father objected to her career choice. She then adopted her maternal surname, Vélez, as her stage name. Her performances in Mexican vaudeville earned her recognition, and she was soon discovered by American producers. In 1926, she traveled to Los Angeles, where she met comedian Fanny Brice, who promoted her career as a dancer and recommended her to Flo Ziegfeld.

Lupe's film career took off in 1927 with a small role in the comic Laurel and Hardy short Sailors, Beware!, followed by her breakthrough role in The Gaucho, alongside Douglas Fairbanks. She quickly became known for her explosive screen persona, playing "exotic" or "ethnic" women that were volatile and hot-tempered. Her accent, which was initially thought to be a hindrance, proved to be no barrier in the transition to sound films.

Throughout the 1930s, Lupe appeared in a series of successful comedic films, including Hot Pepper, Strictly Dynamite, and Hollywood Party. She worked with prominent directors like Cecil B. DeMille and Victor Fleming and co-starred with actors such as Gary Cooper and Edward G. Robinson. In 1932, she took a break from films to perform in the Broadway musical revue Hot-Cha!, and later starred in the musical revue Strike Me Pink.

Lupe's personal life was as colorful as her screen persona. She had several high-profile romances with Hollywood actors, including Gary Cooper, and a stormy marriage with Johnny Weissmuller. Her temper and jealousy in her romantic relationships were well-documented and often made headlines.

In the 1940s, Lupe's popularity peaked with the Mexican Spitfire film series, in which she played Carmelita Fuentes, a fiery and charming Mexican singer. The series, which consisted of eight films, cemented her status as a Hollywood star. She continued to appear in films, including Ladies' Day and Redhead from Manhattan, and returned to Mexico to star in an adaptation of Émile Zola's novel Nana.

Lupe's life was cut short when she died of an intentional overdose of the barbiturate drug Seconal on December 14, 1944, at the age of 36. Her death and the circumstances surrounding it were the subject of speculation and controversy. Despite her tumultuous life and career, Lupe Vélez remains a beloved and iconic figure in Hollywood history, known for her fiery personality, captivating on-screen presence, and enduring legacy as "The Mexican Spitfire."

title: Kevin De Bruyne
text:
Kevin De Bruyne is a Belgian professional footballer widely regarded as one of the best players in the world. Born on June 28, 1991, De Bruyne began his youth career at KVV Drongen in 1997, before joining KAA Gent two years later. His early coaches at Gent, Jan Troos and Charly Musonda, focused on developing his technique, including basics, passing, shooting, and dribbling. De Bruyne credits their individual coaching for having a great impact on his development.

In 2005, De Bruyne moved to Genk, where he continued to develop his skills and was eventually promoted to the first team squad in 2008. He made his first-team debut for Genk in a 3-0 defeat at Charleroi on May 9, 2009. De Bruyne established himself as a regular player for Genk, scoring five goals and making 16 assists in 32 league matches during the 2010-11 season, which ended with Genk being crowned Belgian champions.

In January 2012, De Bruyne joined English club Chelsea for a reported fee of £7 million, signing a five-and-a-half-year contract. However, he was loaned back to Genk for the remainder of the 2011-12 season. De Bruyne made his debut for Chelsea in a friendly match against Seattle Sounders FC in July 2012.

In August 2012, De Bruyne joined Werder Bremen on a season-long loan deal from Chelsea. He scored his first goal for Bremen in a 3-2 defeat to Hannover 96 on September 15, 2012. De Bruyne continued to impress during his loan spell, scoring in Bremen's next game, a 2-2 draw with VfB Stuttgart.

After his successful loan spell, De Bruyne returned to Chelsea, but soon moved to VfL Wolfsburg in January 2014 for a fee of £18 million. During his time at Wolfsburg, De Bruyne established himself as one of the best players in the Bundesliga, scoring 10 goals and providing 21 assists in the 2014-15 season, a new Bundesliga record.

In August 2015, De Bruyne joined Manchester City for a reported club-record fee of £54 million. He made his debut for City in a 4-1 win over Ipswich Town in the League Cup and quickly established himself as a key player for the club. De Bruyne has since won numerous titles with City, including the Premier League, FA Cup, League Cup, and UEFA Champions League.

De Bruyne has also been an important player for the Belgian national team, earning 110 caps and scoring 30 goals. He has represented Belgium at several major tournaments, including the 2014 FIFA World Cup, UEFA Euro 2016, and the 2018 World Cup.

Throughout his career, De Bruyne has received numerous individual awards and accolades, including the Premier League Playmaker of the Season, PFA Players' Player of the Year, and UEFA Champions League Midfielder of the Season. He has also been named in the UEFA Champions League Squad of the Season and IFFHS Men's World Team six times each.

De Bruyne's impressive performances have also earned him a place on the shortlist for the Ballon d'Or award, finishing third in 2022 and fourth in 2023. With his exceptional skills and achievements, De Bruyne is widely regarded as one of the best midfielders in the world.

title: Rebecca Romijn
text:
Rebecca Romijn is an American actress and former model, born on November 6, 1972, in Berkeley, California. Her mother, Elizabeth, is a community college instructor of English as a Second Language, and her father, Jaap, is a custom furniture maker. Her father is a native of the Netherlands, and her mother is an American of Dutch descent. Romijn's early life was marked by insecurity, as she was a "drama geek" in her teens and suffered from scoliosis. She studied music at the University of California, Santa Cruz, but eventually pursued a career in fashion modeling.

Romijn's modeling career took off in 1991, and she went on to appear on the covers of numerous top fashion magazines, including Elle, Cosmopolitan, and Sports Illustrated. She also worked with top designers such as Giorgio Armani, Sonia Rykiel, and Anna Molinari, walking the runway alongside models like Claudia Schiffer and Cindy Crawford. In addition to her modeling work, Romijn hosted MTV's House of Style from 1998 to 2000 and appeared in several advertising campaigns, including ones for Escada, Christian Dior, and Maybelline.

Romijn's acting career began to take off in the early 2000s, with her breakout role as Mystique in the X-Men film series. She appeared in X-Men, X2, and X-Men: The Last Stand, showcasing her ability to transform into the character with the help of makeup and prosthetics. She also starred in films like Femme Fatale, The Punisher, and Godsend, and had a recurring role on the ABC series Ugly Betty as Alexis Meade, a transgender woman and sister of the lead character.

In addition to her film and television work, Romijn has also made headlines for her personal life. She was married to actor John Stamos from 1998 to 2005, and later married actor Jerry O'Connell in 2007. The couple has twin daughters, born in 2008. Romijn has been open about her experiences with pregnancy and motherhood, and has used her platform to advocate for various social causes.

Throughout her career, Romijn has demonstrated her versatility as an actress, taking on a range of roles in film and television. She has appeared in a variety of genres, from superhero blockbusters to romantic comedies, and has worked with top directors and actors. In recent years, Romijn has continued to expand her acting resume, appearing in the TNT series The Librarians and the CBS series Star Trek: Discovery. She has also reprised her role as Mystique in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, with a upcoming appearance in Avengers: Doomsday.

Romijn's passion for music has also been evident throughout her career. She has recorded a cover of Prince's "Darling Nikki" and has been featured on the song "Color Me Love" for RuPaul's album Realness. Her love of music has been a constant source of inspiration for her, and she has spoken about the importance of creative expression in her life.

Overall, Rebecca Romijn is a talented and versatile actress who has made a lasting impact on the entertainment industry. From her early days as a model to her current work as an actress, she has consistently demonstrated her range and dedication to her craft. With her upcoming appearance in Avengers: Doomsday and her continued work in film and television, Romijn is sure to remain a beloved and respected figure in the entertainment industry for years to come.

title: Dennis Andersson
text:
Dennis Andersson is a former Swedish motorcycle speedway rider, born on June 3, 1991. He had a successful career in various European countries, including Poland and the UK. Andersson began his career in Poland, riding for Atlas Wrocław in the Polish Speedway Ekstraliga from an unspecified date until the end of the 2012 season. He then went on to ride for Stal Rzeszów for one season in 2013, before completing his final season in Poland with Polonia Bydgoszcz.

In addition to his Polish league appearances, Andersson also rode in the UK, making his British league debut in 2011 for the Poole Pirates. He spent a total of three seasons with the club. Andersson's achievements include winning the 2010 Under-19 European Champion title, a notable victory that showcased his skills as a young rider. He also won the Swedish U-21 Championship on two occasions, in 2010 and 2012.

Andersson's performances in European Championships were also impressive. In the Individual U-19 European Championship, he participated in several events between 2008 and 2010. In 2008, he finished 7th in Stralsund with 9 points, and in 2009, he repeated this finish in Tarnów with 8 points. However, in 2010, he achieved a breakthrough, becoming the Under-19 European Champion in Goričan with 14+3 points.

In team events, Andersson helped Sweden finish runner-up in the 2009 Team U-19 European Championship in Holsted, where he scored 8 points. Throughout his career, Andersson demonstrated his talent and dedication to the sport, earning recognition and accolades in various competitions. His achievements serve as a testament to his skills as a motorcycle speedway rider.

title: Aditya Kalyanpur
text:
Aditya Kalyanpur is a renowned Indian Tabla Maestro born on July 21, 1978, in Mumbai, India. He belongs to the prestigious Punjab gharana and began his musical journey at the tender age of five under the guidance of the legendary Tabla Maestro Alla Rakha Khan and his son Zakir Hussain. This early start laid the foundation for Kalyanpur's future success in the world of music.

As a young tabla player, Kalyanpur gained recognition for his debut performance with his guru Zakir Hussain for the Wah Taj! commercial when he was just 11 years old. His style of playing is characterized by bold and clear execution of syllables, pinpoint precision in rhythm, and a vast repertoire of compositions and improvisational techniques.
