In 2016, Boorman was involved in a serious accident while test riding a motorbike in Portugal, which left him with broken legs and a hip injury. However, he has since recovered and continues to be involved in various projects, including presenting Motorbike TV, a motorcycle magazine entertainment show.

Throughout his career, Boorman has worked with producer Russ Malkin on several projects, including Long Way Round and Extreme Frontiers. He has also written several books, including Long Way Round and Long Way Back, an autobiography. With his friend Ewan McGregor, Boorman continues to embark on exciting journeys, documenting their experiences for television and books.

title: Salt Bae
text:
Nusret Gökçe, better known as Salt Bae, is a Turkish butcher, chef, and restaurateur who gained international fame for his unique technique of preparing and seasoning meat. Born in 1983 in a village in Erzurum Province, Turkey, to a Kurdish family, Gökçe's early life was marked by financial struggles, which forced him to leave school in the sixth grade to work as a butcher's apprentice in Istanbul. His father, Faik, was a mineworker, and Gökçe's exposure to the food industry from a young age likely influenced his future career.

Gökçe's career took off in 2010 when he opened his first restaurant in Istanbul, and later, a restaurant in Dubai in 2014. However, it was in January 2017 that he became a viral sensation, known as Salt Bae, after a series of videos and memes showed him "suavely" cutting meat and sprinkling salt in a unique way. The videos, posted on social media, quickly racked up millions of views, and Gökçe's profile expanded enormously, with many celebrities and politicians visiting his restaurants.

The viral sensation led to the expansion of Gökçe's restaurant chain, Nusr-Et, which now has branches in several countries, including Turkey, Greece, the United States, the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia. The name of the restaurant chain comes from Gökçe's own name and "et," which means "meat" in Turkish. Despite the international fame, Gökçe's restaurants have received mixed reviews, with some critics describing the food as overpriced and lacking flavor. For instance, early reviews of his New York City steakhouse in 2018 were generally negative, with critics calling it "Public Rip-off No. 1" and describing the steak as "mundane" and the hamburgers as "overcooked."

Gökçe has been involved in several controversies throughout his career. In 2017, he was criticized for posing in front of a photo of former Cuban president Fidel Castro. In 2018, a fire broke out at one of his restaurants in Istanbul, injuring several people, including a Czech internet personality who suffered 35% total body surface area burns. Gökçe has also faced criticism for serving food to Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro, amidst food shortages in Venezuela, and for allegedly taking a share of his employees' tips. In 2020, his restaurant in Boston was ordered to close due to COVID-19 safety violations, and in 2022, he was investigated by FIFA for disturbing players and handling the trophy after the World Cup final.

In addition to his restaurant empire, Gökçe has been involved in charitable work, including building a school in his hometown of Erzurum. He has also stated that he has built a library, a guest house, a mosque, an English education center, and a computer laboratory in the town. Gökçe's philanthropic efforts demonstrate a commitment to giving back to his community, and his rags-to-riches story is an inspiration to many. Despite the controversies surrounding him, Gökçe remains a popular figure, with a loyal following and a reputation for his unique culinary style. His restaurant chain continues to expand, and his name has become synonymous with luxury and fine dining.

title: Michael Douglas
text:
Michael Kirk Douglas is a renowned American actor and film producer, born on September 25, 1944, in New Brunswick, New Jersey, to actors Kirk Douglas and Diana Dill. His early life was marked by his family's show business background, with his father being a Jewish immigrant from Russia and his mother from Bermuda. Michael's ancestry is a diverse mix of English, Irish, Scottish, Welsh, French, Belgian, and Dutch. He has a younger brother, Joel Douglas, and two paternal half-brothers, Peter Douglas and Eric Douglas.

Douglas attended The Allen-Stevenson School in New York City, Eaglebrook School in Deerfield, Massachusetts, and The Choate Preparatory School in Wallingford, Connecticut. He later received his Bachelor of Arts degree in dramatic art from the University of California, Santa Barbara, where he was the honorary president of the UCSB Alumni Association. During his college years, Douglas studied acting with Wynn Handman at The American Place Theatre in New York City.

Douglas began his film career in the late 1960s, appearing in small roles in films such as Hail, Hero!, Adam at 6 A.M., and Summertree. His breakthrough role came in 1972 when he starred in the TV series The Streets of San Francisco alongside Karl Malden. The show ran for four seasons, and Douglas later credited Malden as a mentor and someone he deeply admired.

In the 1970s, Douglas formed his own independent film production company, Bigstick Productions, Limited. He acquired the rights to the novel One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest from his father and produced the film, which earned him an Academy Award for Best Picture. Douglas continued to produce and act in films, including The China Syndrome, Romancing the Stone, and The Jewel of the Nile.

The 1980s were a significant period for Douglas, with starring roles in films like Fatal Attraction, Wall Street, and Basic Instinct. He received critical acclaim for his portrayal of Gordon Gekko in Wall Street, winning the Academy Award for Best Actor. He reprised this role in the sequel Wall Street: Money Never Sleeps in 2010.

Throughout his career, Douglas has demonstrated his versatility as an actor, taking on a wide range of roles in films like The War of the Roses, Falling Down, The American President, and Traffic. He has worked with prominent directors like Steven Soderbergh, Oliver Stone, and David Fincher. In addition to his film work, Douglas has made appearances on television, including a notable role in the HBO film Behind the Candelabra, for which he won an Emmy Award.

In recent years, Douglas has continued to act in films and television shows, including the Marvel Cinematic Universe as Hank Pym in Ant-Man and the Wasp, Avengers: Endgame, and Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania. He has also starred in the Netflix series The Kominsky Method, for which he received a Golden Globe Award.

Douglas has received numerous accolades for his contributions to the film industry, including two Academy Awards, five Golden Globe Awards, a Primetime Emmy Award, and the Cecil B. DeMille Award. He was honored with the American Film Institute's Lifetime Achievement Award and the David O. Selznick Achievement Award in Theatrical Motion Pictures.

In his personal life, Douglas has been married to actress Catherine Zeta-Jones since 2000, and they have two children together. He is known for his humanitarian and political activism, sitting on the board of the Nuclear Threat Initiative and serving as a United Nations Messenger of Peace.

In 2025, Douglas announced his semi-retirement from acting, citing his age and desire to spend more time with his family. Throughout his illustrious career, Michael Douglas has established himself as a talented and versatile actor, producer, and philanthropist, leaving a lasting impact on the film industry.

title: Douglas Wood (engineer)
text:
Douglas Wood was a construction engineer born on June 30, 1941, in Whyalla, South Australia. He spent his early life in Geelong, where he attended Geelong College and the Gordon Institute of TAFE, graduating as a mechanical engineer. In 1973, Wood left Australia to work in the United States, where he lived in Alamo, California, with his American wife and daughter. He worked for construction company Bechtel Corporation for 25 years, during which time he was involved in project management and building nuclear plants, including the Palo Verde Nuclear Generating station in Arizona.

Wood later formed his own company and moved to Iraq, where he was kidnapped on May 2, 2005, by the Shura Council of the Mujahideen of Iraq while organizing a business deal in Baghdad. Footage of Wood being held by armed captors was broadcast on the Arabic television network al-Jazeera, showing him pleading for his life and urging Australia and the United States to withdraw their troops from Iraq. The kidnappers demanded that troops be withdrawn within 72 hours, and Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer and Wood's brothers made public appeals for his release.

The Australian government, led by Prime Minister John Howard, refused to give in to the kidnappers' demands, stating that they would neither pull troops out nor pay any ransom. Wood's family conducted a public relations campaign to convince the kidnappers that he was a family man who sympathized with their cause. Six weeks after his capture, Wood was rescued by Iraqi army troops from a house in Ghazaliya, with assistance from U.S. forces. The rescue was the result of a routine raid on a suspected weapons cache, and Wood was found to be alive and in good health.

After his rescue, Wood was taken to a medical facility in Baghdad, where he was seen on CNN footage talking to soldiers and sitting up in bed. Prime Minister John Howard acknowledged the efforts of Australia's Muslim community and cleric Sheikh Taj al-Din Alhilali in helping to secure Wood's release. However, Wood later denied that he had ever spoken to Alhilali during his capture.

In the years following his rescue, Wood continued to be involved in the public eye. In 2009, he contacted Prime Minister Kevin Rudd to express concern for the safety of the Iraqi soldiers who had rescued him, claiming that seven of the ten soldiers had been systematically murdered for giving evidence against his kidnappers. As a result, two Iraqi service personnel were granted permanent refugee visas under Australia's humanitarian program.

Wood also spoke publicly about his experiences and his views on nuclear energy. He stated that he would happily live next door to a nuclear power plant and would assist in the development of an Australian nuclear energy industry. However, he also expressed concerns that Australia's engineers and industrial suppliers were under-qualified to build a local plant. Wood had previously worked on the failed feasibility study for the Jervis Bay Nuclear Power Plant, and his comments added to the debate on nuclear energy in Australia.

title: Riccardo Tisci
text:
Riccardo Tisci is an Italian fashion designer born in 1974 in Taranto and raised in Como. He studied at the Design Istituto d’Arte Applicata in Cantù until he was 17, and then graduated from London's Central Saint Martins College of Art and Design in 1999. After completing his education, Tisci worked for several companies, including Puma, Antonio Berardi, and Coccapani, before signing a three-year contract with Ruffo Research, a company that has helped launch the careers of several fashion designers.

In 2004, Tisci's contract with Ruffo Research expired, and he spent time living in India, where he began working on his own collection. He debuted his first Riccardo Tisci Collection for Fall 2005/2006 in an off-calendar show during Milan Fashion Week in September 2004. The following year, in February 2005, Tisci was appointed as the creative director of Givenchy's haute couture, ready-to-wear, and accessories lines. He was brought to Givenchy by LVMH chief operating officer Antonio Belloni and Givenchy chief executive officer Marco Gobbetti, who considered him a "perfect fit" for the brand.

During his 12-year tenure at Givenchy, Tisci transformed the brand, increasing its turnover six-fold. He presented his first Givenchy haute-couture collection in July 2005 during Paris Fashion Week and went on to design costumes for several high-profile projects, including Madonna's Sticky & Sweet Tour in 2008. Tisci also collaborated with artists and musicians, including Marina Abramović, Rihanna, Beyoncé, and Jay-Z.

In 2018, Tisci left Givenchy to become the chief creative officer of Burberry, replacing Christopher Bailey. During his time at Burberry, Tisci aimed to create pieces that walked the line between tradition and modernity with a darkly gothic charm. He collaborated with Vivienne Westwood on a limited-time collection and worked with Nike on several projects. Tisci's tenure at Burberry lasted until September 2022, when he was replaced by English designer Daniel Lee.

Throughout his career, Tisci has been known for his highly stylized runway presentations, which he describes as "very melancholic" and "romantic." He has also been praised for his ability to assert his own style while working within the framework of a brand. Tisci has collaborated with numerous artists and musicians, including curating issues of A-Anna Magazine and Visionaire's RELIGION issue.

In his personal life, Tisci is openly gay and has been involved in several high-profile collaborations and projects outside of fashion. However, in 2025, he was sued for alleged sexual assault in New York. Despite this, Tisci remains a prominent figure in the fashion industry, known for his innovative designs and boundary-pushing collaborations.

title: Zubaira Tukhugov
text:
Zubaira Tukhugov is a Russian mixed martial artist who competed in the Lightweight division of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC). Born on January 15, 1991, Tukhugov began his professional MMA career in 2010, winning his debut tournament, the Pankration Atrium Cup 2, an eight-man one-night event. He compiled a 10-3 record before being signed by the Russian promotion, Fight Nights, where he won all three of his fights, defeating opponents such as Romano De Los Reyes, Harun Kina, and Vaso Bakocevic. During his time with Fight Nights, Tukhugov also competed for Cage Warriors, where he defeated Denys Pidnebesnyi.

In December 2013, Tukhugov signed with the UFC and made his promotional debut against Thiago Tavares at UFC Fight Night: Machida vs. Mousasi. However, Tavares was forced to withdraw due to an injury, and Tukhugov faced UFC newcomer Douglas Silva de Andrade instead, winning the fight via unanimous decision. He went on to face Ernest Chavez at UFC Fight Night: Nelson vs. Story, winning the fight via technical knockout in the first round.

Tukhugov's UFC career was marked by several wins and losses, including a victory over Phillipe Nover at UFC Fight Night 80 and a loss to Renato Moicano at UFC 198. The latter fight was marred by controversy, as Tukhugov suffered a kick to the groin in the first and second rounds, but the referee allowed the fight to continue. Tukhugov was also involved in a series of events that led to his suspension and fine. He was pulled from a fight against Tiago Trator at UFC Fight Night 102 due to a potential anti-doping violation, and was later suspended for two years and fined $10,000 for testing positive for ostarine.

In addition to his UFC career, Tukhugov was also involved in the infamous post-fight melee at UFC 229, where he punched Conor McGregor, leading to a one-year suspension and a $25,000 fine. Tukhugov returned to the UFC in 2019, facing Lerone Murphy at UFC 242, which ended in a split draw. He went on to face Kevin Aguilar at UFC Fight Night 168, winning the fight via TKO in the first round.

Tukhugov's later fights included a loss to Hakeem Dawodu at UFC 253, a win against Ricardo Ramos at UFC 267, and a loss to Joel Álvarez at UFC 284. On February 28, 2023, Tukhugov was released from the UFC roster. Throughout his career, Tukhugov has been involved in several controversies, including the post-fight incident at UFC 229 and his suspension for testing positive for ostarine. Despite these setbacks, Tukhugov has established himself as a formidable lightweight fighter in the UFC.
